definition_zh: 住处；住宿；食宿；调节；适应；和解；容纳空间；便利安排
definition_en: a place to stay, or the act of adjusting something to fit a need or of reaching an agreement
core_image: 把略长的桌子斜着塞进小屋：空间与需要彼此让步、刚好合上
scene: 订房网站上，旅客挑了一间离车站不远的房间。 We booked accommodation near the station for three nights.
sceneCN: 这里 accommodation 指「住处、住宿」（第 1 个义项：旅行期间住的地方）；句意为我们在车站附近订了三晚住宿。

pos.zh: 名词：住处；住宿；食宿；调节；和解；便利安排

derivatives.zh: 本词去掉名词后缀得到的动词，义为「容纳；为……提供住处；迁就」
由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「乐于助人的；随和的」
由本词加后缀 -ive 构成，义为「调节性的；愿意配合的」
由否定前缀 un- 加 accommodating 构成，义为「不配合的；不肯通融的」

senses.title: A place to stay
senses.definition: a place where someone can stay, especially while travelling or living away from home
senses.definitionCN: 指可以住下的地方，尤指旅行或离家期间
senses.example: The price includes accommodation and breakfast.
senses.exampleCN: 价格包含住宿和早餐。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to fit; a room that fits a traveller is the most concrete result of that fitting.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词意为「使合适」；一间刚好容下旅人的房间，就是这种「合适」最具体的结果。

senses.title: Lodging together with meals
senses.definition: a place to stay together with meals provided, often as part of a job or a course
senses.definitionCN: 指提供膳食的住处，常作为工作或课程的一部分
senses.example: The job comes with free accommodation and meals.
senses.exampleCN: 这份工作提供免费食宿。
senses.why: Fitting a person means fitting the whole person: a bed alone leaves hunger outside the arrangement.
senses.whyCN: 安置一个人就是安置完整的人：只给一张床，饥饿仍被留在安排之外。

senses.title: The act of adjusting to fit
senses.definition: the act of changing something, or of changing oneself, so that it fits a new condition
senses.definitionCN: 指改变某物或改变自身，使之适应新条件的行为
senses.example: Good accommodation to a new school takes time.
senses.exampleCN: 适应一所新学校需要时间。
senses.why: The core meaning is fitting: whenever two things must fit, one of them has to give a little.
senses.whyCN: 核心义就是「相合」：凡两样东西要合在一起，其中一样总要让一点。

senses.title: An agreement reached by adjustment
senses.definition: an arrangement in which two sides each accept less than they wanted, so that they can work together
senses.definitionCN: 指双方各自少要一点、从而能够共事的安排
senses.example: The two sides reached an accommodation after a long night of talks.
senses.exampleCN: 经过一夜长谈，双方达成了和解。
senses.why: Two positions that do not fit are bent until they do, and the result is an accommodation.
senses.whyCN: 两个合不上的立场被弯一弯，直到合上；这个结果就是和解。

senses.title: The eye's focusing adjustment
senses.definition: the change in the shape of the lens of the eye so that near or far objects stay in focus
senses.definitionCN: 指眼睛晶状体改变形状，使近处或远处物体保持清晰
senses.example: Accommodation of the lens lets the eye focus on a near page.
senses.exampleCN: 晶状体的调节让眼睛能看清近处的书页。
senses.why: Physiology uses the same word for the body part that changes its shape to fit the distance of an object.
senses.whyCN: 生理学用同一个词，指身体部位改变形状去迎合物体的远近。

senses.title: Rooms and facilities in the plural
senses.definition: in American English, the rooms, buildings, and services provided for guests or residents
senses.definitionCN: 在美式英语中，指为客人或住户提供的房间、建筑与服务设施
senses.example: The hotel has excellent accommodations for families.
senses.exampleCN: 这家旅馆有很适合家庭的住宿设施。
senses.why: What was one act of fitting becomes a set of concrete units you can count.
senses.whyCN: 原本一次「安置」的行为，变成了一组可以一个个数出来的具体单元。

senses.title: Space to hold people or things
senses.definition: the space or capacity available for people, cars, or objects
senses.definitionCN: 指可供人、车辆或物品使用的空间或容量
senses.example: The hall has accommodation for five hundred guests.
senses.exampleCN: 这个大厅能容纳五百位客人。
senses.why: Fitting is finally about space: a place accommodates what it can physically take in.
senses.whyCN: 「相合」说到底关乎空间：一个地方能装下多少，它就能容纳多少。

senses.title: Changes made for a special need
senses.definition: a change in rules, buildings, or equipment made so that a person with a disability can take part on equal terms
senses.definitionCN: 指为了让残障人士平等参与而修改规则、建筑或设备
senses.example: The school made several accommodations for students who need extra time.
senses.exampleCN: 学校为需要额外时间的学生做了几项便利安排。
senses.why: The fitting is now deliberate: the environment is bent so that a person who did not fit is included.
senses.whyCN: 这时的「相合」是有意为之：环境被弯一弯，让原本合不进来的人也被包含进去。

intro.en: Accommodation is built from the Latin word for measure, and its history runs from fitting to lodging.
intro.cn: accommodation 建立在拉丁语表示「尺度」的词上，它的历史从「使相合」一路走到「住宿」。

items.en: Modus meant 'measure, manner', and it also underlies mode and moderate.
items.cn: modus 意为「尺度、方式」，mode 与 moderate 也出自它。

items.en: Com- 'together' plus modus formed commodus, 'measured together, fitting, convenient'.
items.cn: com-「一起」加 modus 构成 commodus，意为「量得合适、方便合用的」。

items.en: Ad- 'to' plus commodare formed accommodare, 'to make fit, adapt', with a further sense of lending.
items.cn: ad-「向」加 commodare 构成 accommodare，意为「使合适、调节」，另有「借出」之义。

items.en: The noun accommodatio meant 'a fitting, an adjustment'; it passed through French and entered English in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 名词 accommodatio 意为「使相合、调节」；它经法语传入，在十六世纪进入英语。

items.en: The lodging sense develops in the eighteenth century, and the American plural for rooms and services becomes common later.
items.cn: 「住宿」义在十八世纪发展出来，美式英语中表示房间与设施的复数用法则在更晚时流行。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms of the same fitting root; the near-meaning group names places to stay and ways of adjusting.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「使相合」词根的各种形式；近义组列出住处与调节、妥协的说法。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to provide room for, to fit in with, or to do someone a favour.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「容纳、为……提供住处、迁就」，也可指帮某人的忙。

entries.definition: Willing to change plans to help other people.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「乐于助人的、随和的」，指愿意改变计划去配合别人。

entries.definition: A formal adjective for something that adjusts or is willing to adjust.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「调节性的、愿意配合的」，语气较正式。

entries.definition: Unwilling to help or to change arrangements for others.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不配合的、不肯通融的」，是 accommodating 加否定前缀构成的反义形式。

entries.definition: A place to sleep, often rented and usually without meals.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「寄宿处」，常指租来的睡觉之处，通常不含膳食。

entries.definition: Buildings for people to live in, especially as a social or official matter.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「住房、住宅」，多从社会或官方角度谈居住建筑。

entries.definition: Rooms provided for people to live in, used especially of soldiers or staff.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「住处、营房」，多指为军人或员工提供的房间。

entries.definition: An agreement in which each side gives up part of what it wanted.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「妥协」，指双方各自放弃部分要求的协议。

entries.definition: The process of changing to suit new conditions, with no idea of lodging.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「适应、改编」，只强调改变以适合新条件，不含住宿义。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin measure word and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语「尺度」词，以及这个词常出现的搭配。

normal.en: modus is measure: accommodation is what has been measured to fit.
normal.cn: modus 是「尺度」：accommodation 就是量过尺寸、刚好合上的东西。

normal.en: The same root gives commodity and commodious.
normal.cn: 同一词根还给出 commodity 与 commodious。

normal.en: Hotel accommodation is a room measured to fit a guest.
normal.cn: hotel accommodation 就是一间量好尺寸、刚好容下客人的房间。

normal.en: To reach an accommodation is to bend until two sides fit.
normal.cn: to reach an accommodation 就是弯一弯，让两边合上。

normal.en: The American plural accommodations counts the rooms one by one.
normal.cn: 美式复数 accommodations 把房间一间一间数出来。

abstract.en: A table and a small room: neither changes its nature, but one turns and both fit.
abstract.cn: 一张桌子和一间小屋：谁都没有改变本性，只是一转，两边就合上了。

abstract.en: The word covers a bed, a deal, an eye and a wheelchair ramp, because all four are ways of making things fit.
abstract.cn: 这个词涵盖一张床、一项协议、一只眼睛和一条轮椅坡道，因为四者都是让东西合上的办法。

abstract.en: Accommodation always costs a little space or a little pride, and that is why it works.
abstract.cn: 「相合」总要让出一点空间或一点自尊，也正因如此它才成立。

examples.cn: 价格包含住宿和早餐。

examples.en: The two sides reached an accommodation after a long night of talks.
examples.cn: 经过一夜长谈，双方达成了和解。

examples.en: Accommodation of the lens lets the eye focus on a near page.
examples.cn: 晶状体的调节让眼睛能看清近处的书页。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿康莫德申」——把桌椅挪一挪，刚好塞进屋里：住宿、调节、和解。

root: 拉丁语 accommodare「使合适」由 ad-「向」加 commodare「使合用」构成，后者来自 commodus「合适的」，而 commodus 是 com- 加 modus「尺度」构成的。

sensesIntro.en: Accommodation starts from the idea of measuring two things so that they fit, then becomes a room, a meal, an agreement, an eye movement, and a change made for someone's needs.
sensesIntro.cn: accommodation 从「量一量、让两样东西合上」出发，随后变成一间房、一顿饭、一份和解、一次眼睛的调节，以及为某人需要所做的改动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a table slightly too long is turned askew and slides into a small room.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张略长的桌子斜过来一放，刚好滑进小屋。

branches.en: THE ROOM: a place measured to hold a traveller, with or without meals.
branches.cn: 房间线：量好尺寸、刚好容下旅人的地方，供餐或不供餐。

branches.en: THE ADJUSTMENT: a person changes to a new school, and a lens changes for a near page.
branches.cn: 调节线：人适应新学校，晶状体适应近处的书页。

branches.en: THE DEAL: two positions bend until they fit and an agreement appears.
branches.cn: 协议线：两个立场各弯一点，直到合上，协议随之出现。

branches.en: THE UNITS: the plural turns one act of fitting into countable rooms and services.
branches.cn: 单元线：复数把一次「安置」变成可以计数的房间与服务。

branches.en: THE CAPACITY: space to take people in, and deliberate changes so that more people fit.
branches.cn: 容量线：能装下人的空间，以及为了让更多人合进来而做的特意改动。

intro.en: Accommodation is a Latin verb turned noun, with the prefix, the measure root and a long noun ending.
intro.cn: accommodation 是由拉丁语动词转成的名词，由前缀、「尺度」词根和较长的名词后缀组成。

latinIntro.en: Latin modus, commodus, accommodare and accommodatio are all recorded members of one family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 modus、commodus、accommodare 与 accommodatio 都是同一词族中有记录的形式。

items.meaningCN: 使相合；量好尺寸的地方
items.exampleCN: 我们找到了便宜的住处。
modus 是表示「尺度」的词根。
commodus 由 com- 与 modus 组合而成。

items.example: The hall can accommodate two hundred people.
items.exampleCN: 这个大厅能容纳两百人。

definition_zh: 恐慌；惊慌；经济恐慌；惊慌失措
definition_en: a sudden overpowering fear that stops clear thought, a widespread fright in a market or crowd, and to act in such fear
core_image: 灯忽然灭掉的剧场里，人群同时转身挤向同一个门口
scene: 剧场里的灯忽然全灭，前排的人先站起来，后排跟着往门口挤。 A shout from the back turned the whole crowd into a panic.
sceneCN: 这里 panic 是「群体性恐慌」（第 1 个义项：骤然袭来的强烈恐惧）；句意为后排的一声喊叫让整群人陷入恐慌。图中可辨识物件：熄灭的顶灯、挤向出口的人影、翻倒的座椅。

derivatives.zh: panic 加 -y 构成，指容易惊慌的、慌慌张张的
panic 加 -ed 构成，指惊慌失措的
panic 与 stricken 复合而成，指被恐慌击中的

senses.title: A sudden overpowering fear
senses.definition: a sudden, overwhelming feeling of fear that stops people from thinking clearly
senses.definitionCN: 骤然袭来、压倒一切的恐惧，使人无法清楚思考
senses.example: A shout from the back turned the whole crowd into a panic.
senses.exampleCN: 后排一声喊叫让整群人陷入恐慌。
senses.why: The word comes from the god Pan, whose sudden cries in the hills were said to terrify travellers, so the sense begins with fear that arrives with no visible cause.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自牧神潘，据说他在山野里突然发出的叫声会让旅人惊恐，所以词义一开始就是「找不到明确来由的骤然恐惧」。

senses.title: A widespread fright in a market
senses.definition: a sudden loss of confidence that makes many people sell, withdraw or flee at the same moment
senses.definitionCN: 信心骤然崩塌，使许多人在同一时刻抛售、取钱或逃离
senses.example: A rumour about the bank set off a panic among small savers.
senses.exampleCN: 关于那家银行的传言在小储户中引发了一场恐慌。
senses.why: When many people feel the same sudden fear, the word moves from one heart to a whole market: everyone runs at once, and the running itself makes the danger worse.
senses.whyCN: 当许多人同时感到同一种骤然的恐惧，这个词就从一颗心移到一个市场：所有人一起奔跑，而奔跑本身又让危险更大。

senses.title: To act with blind fear
senses.definition: to be so frightened that you act without thinking, or to make other people behave that way
senses.definitionCN: 害怕到不假思索地行动，或使别人也这样行动
senses.example: She panicked when she could not find her passport at the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 在登机口找不到护照时，她一下子慌了。
senses.why: The verb turns the noun into behaviour: the fear takes over the body, and the flailing that follows is the word in action.
senses.whyCN: 动词把这个名词变成行为：恐惧接管了身体，随后那阵手忙脚乱就是这个词的具体样子。

intro.en: Panic comes from the Greek god Pan; a sudden terror in lonely places was called panikon deima, the fear sent by Pan, and the word reached English through French.
intro.cn: panic 来自希腊牧神潘；荒野中骤然袭来的恐惧被称作 panikon deima，即「潘送来的恐惧」，这个词经法语进入英语。

items.en: Pan was the god of shepherds and wild country, and a sudden cry in the hills was said to come from him.
items.cn: 潘是牧人与荒野之神，山间突然响起的叫声被说成是他发出的。

items.en: Greek panikon, short for panikon deima, named the sudden terror that seized travellers in lonely places.
items.cn: 希腊语 panikon 是 panikon deima 的简称，指在荒野中突然攫住旅人的恐惧。

items.en: Late Latin borrowed the Greek adjective as panicus; it is a loan, not an inherited Latin word.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语把希腊形容词借作 panicus；这是借词，不是拉丁语固有词。

items.en: French panique carried the word into English, where it first named fear without a visible cause.
items.cn: 法语 panique 把这个词带进英语，最初指找不到可见原因的恐惧。

items.en: Modern English uses panic for personal fear and for market runs, and spells the past tense panicked with a k to keep the hard sound.
items.cn: 现代英语用 panic 指个人恐惧与市场挤兑，过去式写作 panicked，加 k 以保住硬音。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the English forms built on this noun; the near-meaning group gathers other names for intense fear.
note.cn: 形近组沿这个名词所造的英语形式展开；近义组收其他表示强烈恐惧的说法。

entries.definition: Easily frightened and unable to stay calm; panic plus -y.
entries.definitionCN: 容易受惊、无法保持镇定的；panic 加 -y。

entries.definition: Seized by panic, or the past tense of the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 被恐慌攫住的，或动词的过去式。

entries.definition: Overcome by panic, often used of a crowd or a face.
entries.definitionCN: 被恐慌击中的，常形容人群或脸色。

entries.definition: The general feeling that danger is near.
entries.definitionCN: 感到危险临近的普遍情绪。

entries.definition: Very great fear, stronger and longer than a fright.
entries.definitionCN: 极度的恐惧，比一时的惊吓更强也更久。

entries.definition: Sudden fear caused by a real or expected danger.
entries.definitionCN: 由真实或预期危险引起的骤然恐惧。

entries.definition: A short, sharp feeling of fear.
entries.definitionCN: 短促而尖锐的惊吓。

normalIntro.en: The word carries the name of a god and the shape of a Greek phrase, and its English forms have to protect one hard sound.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词带着一位神的名字和一句希腊短语的形状，它的英语形式还得护住一个硬音。

normal.en: Pan was said to shout in lonely hills, and panic still means fear with no visible cause.
normal.cn: 据说潘会在荒野里突然叫喊，而 panic 至今仍指找不到可见原因的恐惧。

normal.en: The Greek phrase was panikon deima, the terror of Pan, and English cut it down to one word.
normal.cn: 希腊短语是 panikon deima，即「潘的恐惧」，英语把它压缩成了一个词。

normal.en: Panicked doubles the k so the c keeps its hard sound, unlike the wrong spelling paniced.
normal.cn: panicked 双写 k，让 c 保持硬音，而错误的拼写 paniced 做不到。

normal.en: Panic buying empties shelves before the storm has even arrived.
normal.cn: 恐慌性抢购在风暴还没到之前就把货架清空了。

normal.en: A panic attack is the old flight response running with nothing to run from.
normal.cn: 恐慌发作是古老的逃跑反应在空转，根本没有东西可逃。

abstract.en: Panic is fear that spreads faster than the news that caused it.
abstract.cn: 恐慌是一种比引发它的消息传得更快的恐惧。

abstract.en: A crowd in panic is many people obeying the same blind instruction.
abstract.cn: 陷入恐慌的人群，是许多人在服从同一条看不见的指令。

abstract.en: The god is gone, but the sudden shout in the hills is still inside the word.
abstract.cn: 神已经不在了，但山间那声骤然的喊叫仍留在这个词里。

examples.en: A shout from the back turned the whole crowd into a panic.
examples.cn: 后排一声喊叫让整群人陷入恐慌。

examples.en: A rumour about the bank set off a panic among small savers.
examples.cn: 关于那家银行的传言在小储户中引发了一场恐慌。

examples.en: She panicked when she could not find her passport at the gate.
examples.cn: 在登机口找不到护照时，她一下子慌了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕你咳」——一慌就怕你咳出声来，越慌越乱；记住 panic 是恐慌。

root: 希腊神话牧神潘（Pan）；希腊语 panikon deima 意为「潘带来的恐惧」，经晚期拉丁语 panicus、法语 panique 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The core is fear with no clear cause; the senses spread from one person's sudden terror to a whole market running, and then to the behaviour that follows.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是找不到明确来由的恐惧；义项从一个人的骤然惊恐，扩到整个市场的奔逃，再落到随之而来的失控行为。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a theatre going dark and a crowd turning toward one door at the same instant.
core.cn: 核心意象：灯灭的剧场里，人群在同一瞬间转身挤向同一扇门。

branches.en: a theatre darkening without warning
branches.cn: 没有预兆就暗下来的剧场

branches.en: a traveller running from a cry in the hills
branches.cn: 旅人听着山里的喊声拔腿就跑

branches.cn: 储户在银行门口排队

branches.en: a passenger searching for a lost passport
branches.cn: 乘客翻找丢失的护照

branches.en: shelves emptied and a crowd pushing at one door
branches.cn: 被扫空的货架与挤在同一扇门前的人群

intro.en: The word is a Greek name and phrase reshaped by Latin and French, and English then builds three more forms on the noun.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个希腊神名与短语，经拉丁语和法语改写，英语又在名词上造出三个形式。

latinIntro.en: Late Latin panicus is only a borrowing of Greek panikos, so no inherited Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 晚期拉丁语的 panicus 只是对希腊语 panikos 的借用，所以这个词没有可靠的拉丁固有同族词。

items.meaning: god of shepherds and wild places

definition_zh: 柱；专栏；一列
definition_en: a tall stone post that holds up a building, a regular article in a newspaper, or a line of people or things one behind another
core_image: 一根笔直撑起屋顶的高石柱
scene: 古老的剧院门前立着一排高大的石柱。 A white column still stands at the temple gate.
sceneCN: 这里 column 指「柱」（第 1 个义项：支撑建筑的石柱）；句意是神庙门口仍立着一根白色石柱。

derivatives.zh: 专栏作家
柱状的
有柱子的

senses.title: A supporting post
senses.definition: a tall stone or wooden post that holds up part of a building
senses.definitionCN: 支撑建筑某部分的高石柱或木柱
senses.example: The roof rests on six columns.
senses.exampleCN: 屋顶由六根柱子支撑。
senses.why: The Latin word meant the top of a pillar, the part that carries the weight.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词指柱子的顶端，即承重的部分。

senses.title: A regular newspaper piece
senses.definition: a regular article on one subject in a newspaper or magazine
senses.definitionCN: 报刊上关于某一主题的定期文章
senses.example: She writes a weekly column on food.
senses.exampleCN: 她写每周一篇的美食专栏。
senses.why: Print set text in narrow vertical strips, and the page gave the article its name.
senses.whyCN: 印刷把文字排成窄长的竖条，版面便给了这篇文章名字。

senses.title: A line of people or things
senses.definition: a line of people or things standing or arranged one behind another
senses.definitionCN: 人或物前后排成的一列
senses.example: A column of smoke rose from the hill.
senses.exampleCN: 山上升起一柱烟。
senses.why: A pillar is tall and narrow, so anything in a narrow line takes the shape.
senses.whyCN: 柱子又高又窄，于是任何窄长的一列都沿用这个形状。

intro.en: Column comes from Latin columna, a pillar, from columen, the top or summit.
intro.cn: column 出自拉丁语 columna（柱），更早是 columen（顶端、屋脊）。

items.en: Columen meant the top or ridge of a roof.
items.cn: columen 指屋顶的顶端或屋脊。

items.en: Columna named the pillar that held the roof up.
items.cn: columna 指撑起屋顶的柱子。

items.en: French colomne carried the word toward English.
items.cn: 法语 colomne 把词带向英语。

items.en: Printers used column for a vertical strip of text.
items.cn: 印刷者用 column 指竖排的一条文字。

items.en: The word also names a line of troops or of smoke.
items.cn: 这个词也指一列队伍或一道烟。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words close in spelling, while the meaning group names upright posts and lines.
note.cn: 形近组收的是拼写相近的词，近义组列出直立的柱与成行之物。

entries.definition: a territory ruled by another country
entries.definitionCN: 由他国统治的地区

entries.definition: serious and formal in manner
entries.definitionCN: 神态严肃庄重的

entries.definition: a book, or the amount of space something fills
entries.definitionCN: 书卷；或某物占的空间量

entries.definition: a tall upright post of stone or wood
entries.definitionCN: 高大的石制或木制立柱

entries.definition: a strong upright piece of wood or metal
entries.definitionCN: 坚固的竖直木柱或金属柱

entries.definition: a line of things placed side by side
entries.definitionCN: 并排摆放的一行

normalIntro.en: These hooks stand on the picture of a pillar, then lie down as a strip of print and a line of smoke.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子立在柱子的画面上，再横躺成一条文字与一道烟。

normal.en: Column and colony start alike but grow in different directions.
normal.cn: column 与 colony 开头相似，含义却走向不同方向。

normal.en: The silent n in column comes from the Latin columna.
normal.cn: column 里不发音的 n 来自拉丁语 columna。

normal.en: A pillar holds up a roof, and a printed column holds up a page.
normal.cn: 石柱撑住屋顶，印刷的栏撑住版面。

normal.en: The same tall narrow shape becomes a line of soldiers.
normal.cn: 同一个高而窄的形状变成了行军的队伍。

normal.en: A columnist is the person who fills the column.
normal.cn: columnist 就是填满这个专栏的人。

abstract.en: Picture a temple front of white pillars against blue sky.
abstract.cn: 想象蓝天下一排白色神庙立柱。

abstract.en: Picture one narrow strip of news down a wide page.
abstract.cn: 想象宽大版面上一条窄窄的新闻栏。

abstract.en: Picture a thin line of smoke rising without a bend.
abstract.cn: 想象一道细烟笔直升起。

examples.en: The hall is held up by twelve stone columns.
examples.cn: 大厅由十二根石柱支撑。

examples.en: His column appears in the paper every Friday.
examples.cn: 他的专栏每周五见报。

examples.en: A column of trucks waited at the border.
examples.cn: 一列卡车在边境等候。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 column 记成又高又窄的一条：立起来是石柱，排下去是一列。

root: 源自拉丁语 columna（柱），更早是 columen（顶端、屋脊），后引申为竖排文字、专栏与成列之物。

sensesIntro.en: A tall support first, then a vertical strip of print, and then any narrow line.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是高耸的支撑，再是竖排的一条文字，最后是任何窄长的一列。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a straight tall shape rising from the ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个笔直高耸、从地面升起的形状。

branches.en: The stone post is the oldest and most physical sense.
branches.cn: 石柱义最古老，也最具体。

branches.en: Printing turned the tall shape into a strip of text.
branches.cn: 印刷把这个高长形状变成一条文字。

branches.en: Any narrow line borrows the same vertical image.
branches.cn: 任何窄长的一列都借用同一个竖直意象。

branches.en: A pillar and a line of trucks share one narrow shape.
branches.cn: 石柱与车队共享同一个窄长形状。

branches.en: A printed column is itself a line of words.
branches.cn: 印刷的栏本身就是一行行文字排成的列。

intro.en: The family adds -ist for the writer, -ar and -ed for shape, and compounds from daily print.
intro.cn: 这个词族用 -ist 表写作者，用 -ar 与 -ed 表形状，并有日常印刷中的复合词。

latinIntro.en: Columna and columen are the Latin sources, with no prefix needed for the base.
latinIntro.cn: columna 与 columen 是拉丁语来源，词基本身不需前缀。

items.meaning: more than one pillar, column or line
items.meaningCN: 多根柱子、多个专栏或多列
items.example: The table has four columns of numbers.

items.meaning: a writer of a regular newspaper column
items.example: The columnist answered readers every week.
items.exampleCN: 这位专栏作家每周回答读者提问。

items.example: The rock has a columnar structure.

items.exampleCN: 他们走进一座有柱的大厅。

items.example: The advert took two column inches.
items.exampleCN: 这则广告占了两栏英寸。

items.meaning: a newspaper piece about private lives
items.meaningCN: 报道私人生活的报纸栏目
items.example: The gossip column named no one.
items.exampleCN: 这个八卦专栏没有点名。

items.meaning: the line of bones in the back
items.meaningCN: 背部由骨节连成的一列
items.example: The spinal column protects the nerves.

items.meaning: the post that holds a car's wheel

latinEntries.example: Columna is the direct source of column.
latinEntries.exampleCN: columna 是 column 的直接来源。

latinEntries.example: Columen is the older form behind columna.
latinEntries.exampleCN: columen 是 columna 背后更古老的形式。

definition_zh: 公告；通告；宣布；启事；广播通知
definition_en: a formal public statement or notice that makes information known to a group of people
core_image: 一张贴到公告栏上的纸，路过的人都停下来读
scene: 车站大厅的广播忽然响起，所有人抬头看向上方的屏幕。 A loud announcement told passengers that the last train would leave from platform two.
sceneCN: 这里 announcement 是「广播通知」（第 1 个义项：面向公众发布的正式消息）；句意为一则响亮的广播通知告知乘客，末班车将从二号站台开出。画面里有车站大厅、仰头的人群与上方的屏幕。

pos.zh: 名词：公告；通告；宣布；启事；广播通知

derivatives.zh: 本词的动词形式，义为「宣布；公布」，由拉丁语 annuntiare 经法语进入英语
由 announce 加表示人的后缀 -er 构成，义为「播音员；报幕员」
由 announce 加过去分词后缀构成，义为「已宣布的；公开表明的」

senses.title: A formal public notice
senses.definition: a formal statement or notice that gives information to a group of people
senses.definitionCN: 向一群人提供信息的正式声明或告示
senses.example: The school posted an announcement about the new timetable.
senses.exampleCN: 学校贴出了关于新课程表的公告。
senses.why: Announce plus -ment turns the act of bringing news into the thing that carries the news.
senses.whyCN: announce 加 -ment，把「带消息」的动作变成了承载消息的那个东西。

senses.title: The act of announcing
senses.definition: the act or occasion of making something known, especially when it surprises people
senses.definitionCN: 把某事公开的动作或场合，尤指使人意外的宣布
senses.example: His announcement surprised the whole committee.
senses.exampleCN: 他的宣布让整个委员会都很意外。
senses.why: The suffix -ment can name the action itself as well as its result, so one word covers both.
senses.whyCN: -ment 既能命名动作本身，也能命名动作的结果，因此同一个词兼具两义。

senses.title: A small advertisement or notice
senses.definition: a short notice placed in a newspaper or on a board, often advertising a job or service
senses.definitionCN: 登在报纸或贴在告示板上的短启事，常用于招聘或服务信息
senses.example: She found the job in the announcements at the back of the paper.
senses.exampleCN: 她在报纸后面的启事栏里找到了这份工作。
senses.why: A paid notice is still a public message, and the newspaper simply becomes the room it is read in.
senses.whyCN: 付费启事仍然是公开消息，只是报纸变成了它被读到的那间「房间」。

senses.title: A birth, marriage or death notice
senses.definition: a formal family notice in a newspaper recording a birth, engagement, marriage or death
senses.definitionCN: 登在报纸上的正式家庭启事，公布出生、订婚、结婚或去世
senses.example: They placed a birth announcement in the local paper.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在当地报纸上登了一则出生启事。
senses.why: Private news is given a fixed public form, and that form takes the name of the act.
senses.whyCN: 私人的消息被赋予一个固定的公开形式，这个形式就沿用了「宣布」的名字。

senses.title: A spoken broadcast notice
senses.definition: a message read aloud over a public address system, radio or television
senses.definitionCN: 通过公共广播、电台或电视朗读出来的通知
senses.example: A loud announcement told passengers that the last train would leave from platform two.
senses.exampleCN: 一则响亮的广播通知告知乘客，末班车将从二号站台开出。
senses.why: The audience is scattered but the message arrives at once, which is why broadcasting keeps this word.
senses.whyCN: 听众是分散的，消息却同时抵达，因此广播场景一直沿用这个词。

intro.en: Announcement is the noun built on announce, whose Latin core is a messenger bringing news.
intro.cn: announcement 是建在 announce 上的名词，其拉丁核心是一个带来消息的传信人。

items.en: Nuntius meant 'messenger' and 'message'; the word carries both the bearer and the thing carried.
items.cn: nuntius 兼指「传信人」与「消息」，这个词同时带着送信的人与被送的内容。

items.en: Annuntiare meant 'to bring news to someone, to report', built with ad- 'to' plus nuntiare.
items.cn: annuntiare 意为「把消息带给某人、报告」，由 ad-「向」加 nuntiare 构成。

items.en: Old French anoncier and the noun anonce carried the meaning into the everyday language of courts and towns.
items.cn: 古法语动词 anoncier 与名词 anonce 把这个意思带进宫廷与城镇的日常语言。

items.en: English took the verb announce and formed the noun with -ment; the exact first dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 英语借入动词 announce，并用 -ment 造出名词；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The noun spreads into public administration, newspapers, broadcasting and family notices.
items.cn: 这个名词扩展到公共行政、报纸、广播与家庭启事。

note.en: The look-alike group is the announce family; the near-meaning group gathers public statements of different length and formality.
note.cn: 形近组收 announce 词族；近义组收各类公开声明，篇幅与正式程度不同。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to make information known publicly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「宣布；公布」，指把信息向公众公开。

entries.definition: A person who reads announcements aloud, on radio or at an event.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「播音员、报幕员」，指在电台或活动现场朗读通知的人。

entries.definition: Past participle used as an adjective: made known publicly.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词作形容词，义为「已宣布的、公开表明的」。

entries.definition: A written or printed sign giving information; shorter and less formal than an announcement.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「通知、告示」，指书面或印刷的信息，比 announcement 更短、更不正式。

entries.definition: A formal account of facts or a position, often issued by an organization.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「声明、陈述」，指对事实或立场的正式说明，常由机构发布。

entries.definition: A solemn or official statement, stronger and more binding than an announcement.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「宣告、宣言」，语气庄重、更具约束力，强于 announcement。

entries.definition: A short official news report issued regularly or urgently.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「简报、公告」，指定期或紧急发布的简短官方消息。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the -ment ending and the five places an announcement is actually read.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用 -ment 词尾，以及公告实际被读到的五个场所。

normal.en: Announce plus -ment: the act becomes a thing you can pin to a board.
normal.cn: announce 加 -ment：动作变成了可以钉在告示板上的东西。

normal.en: An announcement is read in a hall, a newspaper, a radio, a station and a family column.
normal.cn: 公告会在礼堂、报纸、电台、车站与家庭启事栏里被读到。

normal.en: Make an announcement is the fixed verb frame; you do not say do an announcement.
normal.cn: make an announcement 是固定动词搭配，不说 do an announcement。

normal.en: Birth announcement turns private family news into a public form.
normal.cn: birth announcement 把私人的家庭消息变成公开形式。

normal.en: An announcer is the person; an announcement is the text or the spoken message.
normal.cn: announcer 是人，announcement 是文本或被读出的消息。

abstract.en: Picture a sheet of paper on a cork board, its corners curling, a line of people stopping to read.
abstract.cn: 想象软木板上的一张纸，四角微微卷起，一队人停下来读。

abstract.en: Picture a voice filling a station hall from hidden speakers, every head lifting at once.
abstract.cn: 想象声音从看不见的喇叭里充满车站大厅，所有头同时抬起。

abstract.en: Picture a small box in a newspaper where a family writes one line of news for strangers.
abstract.cn: 想象报纸里一个小方框，一家人在那里为陌生人写下一行消息。

examples.en: A loud announcement told passengers that the last train would leave from platform two.
examples.cn: 一则响亮的广播通知告知乘客，末班车将从二号站台开出。

examples.en: The school posted an announcement about the new timetable.
examples.cn: 学校贴出了关于新课程表的公告。

examples.en: They placed a birth announcement in the local paper.
examples.cn: 他们在当地报纸上登了一则出生启事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额闹恩斯门特」——额上冒汗、闹哄哄地，把门特大的纸贴出来：公告

root: 拉丁语 nuntius「传信人、消息」加 ad-「向」构成 annuntiare「宣布、报告」，经古法语进入英语为 announce；再加名词后缀 -ment 构成 announcement，指宣布这一动作或其文本。现代扩展到报纸启事、广播播报与家庭公告。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses are one message in five carriers: a posted notice, the act itself, a small advertisement, a family notice, and a spoken broadcast.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项是同一则消息的五种载体：张贴的告示、宣布的动作本身、小启事、家庭公告，以及口头广播。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one sheet of news is placed where a whole group will see it at the same time.
core.cn: 核心意象：一则消息被放到一群人会同时看到的地方。

branches.en: THE NOTICE LINE: the physical or official notice that carries information.
branches.cn: 告示线：承载信息的实体或正式告示。

branches.en: THE ACT LINE: the occasion of making the news known.
branches.cn: 动作线：把消息公开的那个场合本身。

branches.en: THE ADVERTISEMENT LINE: a paid notice in a paper or on a board.
branches.cn: 广告线：报纸或告示板上的付费启事。

branches.en: THE FAMILY LINE: private news given a fixed public form.
branches.cn: 家庭线：私人消息被赋予固定的公开形式。

branches.en: THE SPEAKING LINE: the message read aloud to scattered listeners.
branches.cn: 朗读线：向分散的听众朗读出来的消息。

intro.en: Announcement is a Latin messenger verb plus the English noun suffix -ment, with a French step in between.
intro.cn: announcement 是拉丁语「传信」动词加英语名词后缀 -ment，中间经过法语一步。

latinIntro.en: Nuntius, nuntiare and annuntiare are recorded Latin words, so no reconstruction is involved.
latinIntro.cn: nuntius、nuntiare 与 annuntiare 都是有记录的拉丁词，因此不涉及重构。

items.example: It directs the news toward the audience.
It is the centre of the family.
The noun is built directly on it.

derivatives.zh: 本词的动词形式，义为「宣布；公布」
由 announce 加 -er 构成，义为「播音员；报幕员」

definition_zh: 紧的；牢固的；紧身的；绷紧的；紧缩的；（时间）紧张的
definition_en: held or fixed firmly so that it cannot move, or fitting closely, or with little room in time or money
core_image: 收紧的绳索与贴身的衣料：没有一丝余隙
scene: 行李在车顶晃动，他停车重新固定。 He pulled the straps tight and checked them twice.
sceneCN: 这里 tight 是「拉紧、绷紧」（第 1 个义项：无松弛）；句意：他把带子拉紧并检查了两遍。

pos.zh: 紧的；牢固的；紧身的；紧缩的

derivatives.zh: tight 加 -en，义为「使变紧；拧紧；加强」
tight 加 -ly，义为「紧紧地」
tight 加 -ness，义为「紧；牢固；拮据」
tight + rope 复合，义为「（杂技用的）绷紧的钢丝」

senses.title: Firmly held so it cannot move
senses.definition: fixed or pulled firmly so that there is no looseness or movement
senses.definitionCN: 被固定或拉紧，毫无松脱或晃动
senses.example: Make sure the lid is tight before shaking.
senses.exampleCN: 摇晃前务必确认盖子拧紧了。
senses.why: The core image is cord drawn until no slack remains.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是绳被拉到再无半分松弛。

senses.title: Clothes fitting closely to the body
senses.definition: fitting very closely to the body, without extra room
senses.definitionCN: 紧贴身体，没有多余空间
senses.example: The jacket felt tight across the shoulders.
senses.exampleCN: 这件外套肩部有些紧。
senses.why: Fabric drawn like cord hugs the body with no slack.
senses.whyCN: 布料如绳般收紧，便裹住身体不留余地。

senses.title: Under strict control
senses.definition: controlled firmly, with little freedom or leakage allowed
senses.definitionCN: 受到严格控制，自由或疏漏极少
senses.example: Tight security surrounded the summit.
senses.exampleCN: 峰会四周戒备森严。
senses.why: What is cinched cannot slip; control drawn tight admits nothing.
senses.whyCN: 收紧之物无从滑脱；拉满的控制容不下任何疏漏。

senses.title: With little money
senses.definition: having very little money to spend, or spending as little as possible
senses.definitionCN: 几乎没有可花的钱，或尽量少花钱
senses.example: We are on a tight budget this month.
senses.exampleCN: 这个月我们预算吃紧。
senses.why: Money squeezed like cord leaves no slack for extra spending.
senses.whyCN: 钱被如绳勒紧，花销便没有半点余量。

senses.title: With little time
senses.definition: arranged so that there is very little spare time between events
senses.definitionCN: 安排得几乎没有间隙
senses.example: We have a tight schedule to catch the ferry.
senses.exampleCN: 为赶渡轮，我们的行程排得很紧。
senses.why: Hours packed like a drawn rope leave no gaps.
senses.whyCN: 时间像绷紧的绳一样排满，不留空隙。

senses.title: Close and even in a contest
senses.definition: with opponents so close that the result is hard to predict
senses.definitionCN: 对手之间差距极小，结果难料
senses.example: The election was a tight race to the end.
senses.exampleCN: 这场选举到最后仍难分高下。
senses.why: Two sides pressed against each other like rope pulled from both ends.
senses.whyCN: 双方如两端拉绳，彼此紧贴不分胜负。

senses.title: Close-knit and loyal
senses.definition: describing a group whose members are closely connected and loyal to each other
senses.definitionCN: 形容群体成员关系紧密、彼此忠诚
senses.example: They are a tight team after years together.
senses.exampleCN: 多年磨合后他们是一支很团结的队伍。
senses.why: People bound like cords in a knot cannot easily be pulled apart.
senses.whyCN: 人们如绳结般缠紧，便不易被拆散。

senses.title: Penny-pinching with money
senses.definition: unwilling to spend or lend money
senses.definitionCN: 不愿花钱或借钱
senses.example: He is tight with money and rarely treats anyone.
senses.exampleCN: 他花钱很抠，很少请客。
senses.why: The grip on the purse stays closed, as tight as the knot on a bag.
senses.whyCN: 对钱袋的抓握始终不松，如袋口的死结。

intro.en: Tight comes from the Old Norse thettr, meaning tight and watertight, replacing older English forms. The Germanic root behind it is thik-, to thicken or press close, the same family as thatch.
intro.cn: tight 源自古诺斯语 thettr「紧的、不漏水的」，取代了英语更早的形式。其日耳曼词根为 thik-「使变稠、压紧」，与 thatch 同族。

items.en: The reconstructed root thik- meant to press together or thicken.
items.cn: 重构词根 thik- 意为压合、增稠。

items.en: Thettr described anything drawn firm, including watertight planking.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 thettr 形容任何拉紧之物，包括不漏水的船板。

items.en: English borrowed thight from Norse and it spread through everyday use.
items.cn: 中古英语从诺斯语借入 thight，并在日常使用中铺开。

items.en: Spelling settled as tight, covering firmness of grip, fit and control.
items.cn: 拼写定为 tight，兼指抓握、贴合与控制之紧。

items.en: Modern English added tight budgets, tight schedules and tight races.
items.cn: 现代英语又生预算吃紧、日程紧凑与选情胶着诸义。

note.en: The first group gathers the drawn-firm family; the second lists neighbours in firmness and control.
note.cn: 第一组是「拉紧」家族；第二组列出牢固与控制义的近邻。

entries.definition: a rope stretched tight for walking across at height
entries.definitionCN: 绷紧供高空行走用的钢丝

entries.definition: roof covering pressed close, from the same Germanic root
entries.definitionCN: 茅草屋顶，压紧铺成，与 tight 同根

entries.definition: pulled completely straight, with no slack at all
entries.definitionCN: 拉得笔直、毫无松弛

entries.definition: solid and not yielding when pressed
entries.definitionCN: 坚实、按压不变形

entries.definition: fitting closely and warmly, often comfortably
entries.definitionCN: 贴合温暖，常指舒适

entries.definition: loose and not pulled firm, the direct contrast
entries.definitionCN: 松弛的，与 tight 直接相对

normalIntro.en: Real links: hold tight, a tight budget, a tight schedule, tight security, and sleep tight.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：hold tight、tight budget、tight schedule、tight security，以及 sleep tight。

normal.en: Tight is Norse thettr: anything drawn until no slack is left.
normal.cn: tight 出自古诺斯语 thettr：拉到再无松弛之物。

normal.en: Hold tight means grip until nothing can pull you free.
normal.cn: hold tight 意为抓到什么都拽不走你。

normal.en: A tight budget leaves no spare coin, like no spare rope.
normal.cn: tight budget 不留闲钱，如绳不留余头。

normal.en: Sleep tight wishes you a bed tucked as firm as a drawn sheet.
normal.cn: sleep tight 祝你的床铺如拉平的床单般安稳。

normal.en: Tighten adds the verb ending: to draw the rope one notch further.
normal.cn: tighten 加上动词词尾：把绳再拧紧一格。

abstract.en: Firmness is simply distance removed.
abstract.cn: 牢固不过是把余隙清空。

abstract.en: What is drawn tight holds, and what holds may also squeeze.
abstract.cn: 绷紧者能抓住，抓住者也可能勒住。

abstract.en: Scarcity tightens both purses and clocks.
abstract.cn: 匮乏同时勒紧钱袋与时钟。

examples.en: She gripped the rail tight as the bus turned.
examples.cn: 转弯时她紧紧抓住扶手。

examples.en: These shoes are too tight for long walks.
examples.cn: 这双鞋太紧，不适合久走。

examples.en: The new rules tightened control on spending.
examples.cn: 新规收紧了支出管控。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「太贴」——衣服「太贴」身、绳「太贴」物，没有一丝松弛 → tight 紧的

root: 古诺斯语 þéttr「紧的、不漏水的」→ 中古英语 thight → tight；上溯日耳曼词根 *þik-「压紧、增稠」，与 thatch「茅草（压紧的屋顶）」同源。

sensesIntro.en: No-slack firmness spreads from lids and clothes to control, money, time, races, teams and purses.
sensesIntro.cn: 「无松弛的牢固」从瓶盖与衣服蔓延到管控、钱财、时间、赛况、团队与钱袋。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: rope drawn until the last slack is gone.
core.cn: 核心意象：绳被拉到最后一丝松弛消失。

branches.en: Physical firmness on objects and clothes.
branches.cn: 施于物与衣的物理之紧。

branches.en: Control cinched until nothing slips.
branches.cn: 管控收紧，无物漏网。

branches.en: Money and hours squeezed to no slack.
branches.cn: 钱与时间被勒到无余。

branches.en: Opponents pressed evenly like a pulled rope.
branches.cn: 对手如拉绳般均势相抵。

branches.en: Group loyalty knotted close; purse strings knotted shut.
branches.cn: 群体之谊结得紧；钱袋之口结得死。

intro.en: Tight forms compounds and verbs freely; the items show the -en verb and the common pairs.
intro.cn: tight 可自由构成复合词与动词；词条展示 -en 动词及常见搭配。

latinIntro.en: The root is Germanic; no Latin cognates exist.
latinIntro.cn: 词根属日耳曼语源，无拉丁同源词。

items.meaning: a stretched rope for high walking

items.example: An air-tight alibi held up in court.
items.exampleCN: 无懈可击的不在场证明经得起庭审。

items.meaning: to make rules or performance stricter
items.example: They tightened up on late returns.
items.exampleCN: 他们加强了对逾期归还的管理。

items.example: He felt a tightness in his chest.
A tight-fisted boss never gave bonuses.
items.exampleCN: 吝啬的老板从不发奖金。

definition_zh: 航空器；飞机（单复数同形）
definition_en: any vehicle that is designed to travel through the air, such as an airplane, helicopter or glider
core_image: 跑道尽头抬起的机头，轮子刚离开地面的那一瞬
scene: 清晨的停机坪上，一排银灰色机身停在白线内，地勤人员绕着轮子逐一检查。 The ground crew checked every aircraft before the morning departures.
sceneCN: 这里 aircraft 指「航空器」（第 1 个义项：一切能在大气中飞行的载具）；句意为地勤人员在早班起飞前检查了每一架飞机。画面里是停机坪、机身与绕机检查的地勤。

pos.zh: 名词：航空器；飞机（单复数同形）

derivatives.zh: 由 aircraft 加 man 构成，义为「空军（或海军航空）地勤士兵」，是英军的一个军衔称谓
由 aircraft 加 woman 构成，义为「女性航空地勤士兵」，与 aircraftman 相对应
aircraft 加 man 的另一种拼合形式，义为「航空地勤人员」，多见于英国海军航空兵

senses.title: Any vehicle that flies
senses.titleCN: 航空器：会飞的载具总称
senses.definition: any vehicle built to travel through the air, including airplanes, helicopters, gliders and balloons
senses.definitionCN: 任何为在空中航行而制造的载具，包括飞机、直升机、滑翔机与气球
senses.example: The museum displays aircraft from the early years of flight.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆展出了飞行早期的各种航空器。
senses.why: Air marks the medium and craft supplies the old sense of a vessel, so the compound covers every kind of craft that travels in that medium.
senses.whyCN: air 标出介质，craft 在这里取「航行器」的旧义，因此这个复合词能涵盖在这一介质中航行的一切载具。

senses.title: An airplane in everyday use
senses.titleCN: 飞机：日常语境中的具体指称
senses.definition: an airplane, especially when the word is used in counting, schedules or military reports
senses.definitionCN: 飞机，尤用于计数、航班安排或军事报告等语境
senses.example: The airline ordered forty new aircraft for its long-haul routes.
senses.exampleCN: 这家航空公司为长途航线订购了四十架新飞机。
senses.why: Because the fixed-wing airplane is the flying craft people meet most often, the general word is read as 'airplane' whenever nothing else is meant.
senses.whyCN: 固定翼飞机是人们最常接触的飞行载具，所以当上下文没有指别的种类时，这个总称就被直接读作「飞机」。

intro.en: Aircraft is an English compound of two old elements: air, a Greek word that came through Latin and French, and craft, a native word for skill that shifted to mean a vessel.
intro.cn: aircraft 是由两个古老成分构成的英语复合词：air 是经拉丁语与法语传来的希腊词，craft 是本族词，原指技艺，后转指船只。

items.en: Cræft meant 'strength, power, skill, art', a native Germanic noun; the modern word still carries the idea of trained ability.
items.cn: cræft 是日耳曼语本族名词，意为「力量、气力、技艺、手艺」；现代词仍带着「受训能力」的观念。

items.en: Greek aer, the lower misty air, passed through Latin aer and Old French air into English, keeping both the gas sense and the manner sense.
items.cn: 希腊语 aer 指下层带雾的空气，经拉丁语 aer 与古法语 air 进入英语，既保留气体义，也保留神态义。

items.en: Craft acquired the sense of a small vessel in the seventeenth century; how that transfer happened is source uncertain, though it is often linked to the idea of a shaped thing that floats.
items.cn: craft 在十七世纪获得「小船」义；这一转移如何发生，来源不确定，一般认为与「成形而能浮的东西」这一观念有关。

items.en: The compound air-craft is recorded in the nineteenth century for craft that navigate the air, at first balloons and airships rather than powered planes.
items.cn: 复合形式 air-craft 在十九世纪有记录，指在空中航行的载具，最初是气球与飞艇，而不是动力飞机。

items.en: From the early twentieth century the word is applied to powered airplanes, and its plural stays aircraft, unchanged in form.
items.cn: 二十世纪初起，这个词用来指动力飞机，其复数仍是 aircraft，形式不变。

note.en: The first group is made of other compounds with the same -craft element; the second group is made of the flying machines that aircraft covers or is compared with.
note.cn: 第一组是同用 -craft 这一成分的其他复合词；第二组是 aircraft 所涵盖或常与之比较的各种飞行器。

entries.definition: A vehicle built to travel beyond the earth's atmosphere; same -craft element, different medium.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「航天器」，指在地球大气层之外航行的载具；同样用 -craft 成分，只是介质不同。

entries.definition: A boat or other vessel on water, or such vessels as a class; the same craft element with water as the medium.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「水上船只」或这类船只的总称；同样以 craft 为成分，介质换成水。

entries.definition: A vehicle that rides on a cushion of air over land or water; formed with hover plus craft.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「气垫船（或气垫车）」，指靠气垫在地面或水面上行驶的载具，由 hover 加 craft 构成。

entries.definition: A junior rank in some air forces, formed by adding man to aircraft; it names a person, not a vehicle.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指某些空军中的初级军衔，由 aircraft 加 man 构成；它指人，不指载具。

entries.definition: A fixed-wing aircraft driven by engines; the American word for what British English calls an aeroplane.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「飞机」，指有固定机翼、由发动机驱动的航空器；是美式说法，英式作 aeroplane。

entries.definition: The British word for a powered fixed-wing aircraft; a direct borrowing of the French form.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，英式拼写，义为「飞机」，指动力固定翼航空器，直接借自法语形式。

entries.definition: The short everyday word for an airplane; it drops the technical precision of aircraft.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「飞机」，是日常口语的简称，不如 aircraft 精确。

entries.definition: A flying machine with rotating blades that can rise straight up; an aircraft, but not a fixed-wing plane.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「直升机」，靠旋转桨叶垂直起降；属于航空器，但不是固定翼飞机。

entries.definition: An aircraft with no engine that flies on rising air; it shows how wide the class aircraft really is.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「滑翔机」，指没有发动机、靠上升气流飞行的航空器；它说明 aircraft 这个类别有多宽。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the two real halves of the compound and the way English treats its plural.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子用的是这个复合词真实的两半，以及英语处理它复数的方式。

normal.en: Air is the medium, craft is the vessel: put them together and you get a vessel for the air.
normal.cn: air 是介质，craft 是航行器：两者一合，就是「空中的航行器」。

normal.en: Craft already meant a boat before it meant a flying machine, which is why the same word serves ships, planes and spacecraft.
normal.cn: craft 在指飞行器之前先指船，所以同一个词既能用于船，也能用于飞机与航天器。

normal.en: Aircraft carrier is not a flying craft but a ship that carries them.
normal.cn: aircraft carrier 不是会飞的载具，而是载着它们的船。

normal.en: The plural is the same word: one aircraft, ten aircraft.
normal.cn: 复数和单数同形：一架 aircraft，十架还是 aircraft。

normal.en: Aircraftman adds a person to the machine, not another vehicle.
normal.cn: aircraftman 是在机器后面加上一个人，而不是又一种载具。

abstract.en: Picture two old words shaking hands: air, the invisible medium, and craft, the shaped hull that floats in it.
abstract.cn: 想象两个古老的词握手：一个是看不见的介质 air，一个是在其中漂浮的成形船体 craft。

abstract.en: Swap the medium and the same hull sails on water, rises into space or rides a cushion of air.
abstract.cn: 换掉介质，同一具船体就能在水上航行、升入太空，或压在气垫上滑行。

abstract.en: Aircraft keeps its shape in the plural because the class matters more than the count.
abstract.cn: aircraft 的复数不改形，因为这个类别本身比数目更重要。

examples.en: The airline has ordered twenty new aircraft.
examples.cn: 这家航空公司订购了二十架新飞机。

examples.en: Rescue aircraft circled the flooded valley for hours.
examples.cn: 救援飞机在被淹的山谷上空盘旋了数小时。

examples.en: Every aircraft in the fleet was checked before take-off.
examples.cn: 机队里的每一架飞机都在起飞前接受了检查。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱尔克拉夫特」——爱尔（air）在天上，克拉夫特（craft）是船，合起来就是天上的船

root: air 来自希腊语 aer「下层空气」，经拉丁语与古法语进入英语；craft 是古英语 cræft「力量、技艺」，十七世纪起又指「小船」。两者在十九世纪合成 aircraft，指在空中航行的载具，二十世纪起多指飞机。

sensesIntro.en: The word has one core concept, a craft that travels through the air, and English uses it in two ways: as the whole class of flying vehicles, and in everyday counting and reports where it simply means airplanes.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词只有一个核心概念——在空中航行的载具；英语把它用在两个层面：一是涵盖所有飞行器的总称，二是在日常计数与报告中直接指飞机。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shaped hull lifted off the runway, made for one medium only, the air.
core.cn: 核心意象：一具成形的机体离开跑道，只为一个介质而生，那就是空气。

branches.en: THE CLASS: air plus craft names every vehicle that travels in that medium, from balloon to helicopter.
branches.cn: 类别线：air 加 craft，命名一切在该介质中航行的载具，从气球到直升机。

branches.en: THE MEDIUM: swapping air for space or water produces spacecraft and watercraft from the same second element.
branches.cn: 介质线：把 air 换成 space 或 water，同一个第二成分就生出 spacecraft 与 watercraft。

branches.en: THE COUNT: the plural never changes, because the class is being named even when single machines are counted.
branches.cn: 计数线：复数从不改形，因为即便在数单架机器时，被命名的仍是这个类别。

branches.en: THE DEFAULT: in schedules and fleet reports the most common member of the class takes over the whole word.
branches.cn: 默认线：在航班表与机队报告里，这个类别中最常见的成员替代了整个词。

branches.en: THE PERSON: adding man or woman shifts the compound from the machine to the people who service it.
branches.cn: 人物线：加上 man 或 woman，复合词就从机器转指维护机器的人。

intro.en: Aircraft is a native compound, so its parts are ordinary English elements rather than Latin affixes.
intro.cn: aircraft 是英语本土复合词，它的构件是普通英语成分，而不是拉丁词缀。

latinIntro.en: Only the air half has a Latin record, borrowed from Greek aer; craft is Germanic and has no Latin cognate here.
latinIntro.cn: 只有 air 这一半有拉丁语记录，它是从希腊语 aer 借来的；craft 属日耳曼语，在这里没有拉丁同源词。

items.example: It marks what kind of craft is meant.
items.exampleCN: 它标出所指的是哪一种航行器。

items.example: The vessel sense is the one used here.
items.exampleCN: 这里用的是「船只、航行器」这一义。

items.meaning: a vehicle of a particular medium
items.exampleCN: 它构成 spacecraft 与 watercraft。
它构成 airline 与 airport。
它构成 airplane 与 seaplane。
它构成 aeroplane 与 aerodynamics。

items.meaning: a person connected with a thing
a female person connected with a thing

definition_zh: 胡须；络腮胡
definition_en: the hair that grows on a man's chin and cheeks
core_image: 老人花白的络腮胡垂到胸前
scene: 炉火映着他的侧脸。 The old man stroked his grey beard.
sceneCN: 这里 beard 是「络腮胡」（第 1 个义项：长在男子下巴与两颊上的毛发）；句意是老人捋了捋花白的胡须。

derivatives.zh: 由 beard 加 -ed 构成，义为「有胡须的」
由 beard 加 -less 构成，义为「无须的」

senses.title: Hair on the face
senses.definition: the hair that grows on a man's chin and cheeks
senses.definitionCN: 长在男子下巴与两颊上的毛发
senses.example: The old man stroked his grey beard.
senses.exampleCN: 老人捋了捋花白的胡须。
senses.why: The word came through French from Latin barba, meaning beard.
senses.whyCN: 这个词经法语来自拉丁语 barba「胡须」。

senses.title: To confront boldly
senses.definition: to face someone or something boldly
senses.definitionCN: 大胆地面对某人或某物
senses.example: He bearded the lion in its den.
senses.exampleCN: 他闯入狮穴公然挑衅。
senses.why: To beard a lion was to seize it by the beard, so the verb came to mean defy.
senses.whyCN: 「抓住狮子的胡须」后来引申为公然对抗。

intro.en: Beard goes back through French to a Latin word for the hair on the face.
intro.cn: beard 经法语可追溯到拉丁语中表示面部毛发的词。

items.en: barba meant a beard.
items.cn: barba 意为「胡须」。

items.en: barbe kept the same meaning.
items.cn: barbe 保留了相同含义。

items.en: the word entered English as berd.
items.cn: 这个词进入英语时写作 berd。

items.en: the spelling became beard.
items.cn: 拼写演变为 beard。

items.en: beard also works as a verb meaning to defy.
items.cn: 如今 beard 也作动词，意为公然对抗。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by one letter; the near-meaning group gives other facial hair.
note.cn: 形近组只差一个字母；近义组是其他面部毛发词。

entries.definition: a small round piece with a hole
entries.definitionCN: 珠子

entries.definition: a food baked from flour
entries.definitionCN: 面包

entries.definition: a large heavy wild animal
entries.definitionCN: 熊

entries.definition: hair above the upper lip
entries.definitionCN: 小胡子

entries.definition: hair on the sides of the face
entries.definitionCN: 胡须

entries.definition: short hair after shaving
entries.definitionCN: 胡茬

normalIntro.en: A beard is the hair on a man's chin and cheeks.
normalIntro.cn: beard 是长在男子下巴与两颊的毛发。

normal.en: The plural is beards.
normal.cn: 复数是 beards。

normal.en: Bearded means having a beard.
normal.cn: bearded 指有胡须的。

normal.en: Beardless means without a beard.
normal.cn: beardless 指无须的。

normal.en: A full beard covers the whole chin.
normal.cn: a full beard 指覆满下巴的络腮胡。

normal.en: Beard the lion means to confront boldly.
normal.cn: beard the lion 指大胆对抗。

abstract.en: See grey hair falling to a chest.
abstract.cn: 想象花白胡须垂到胸前。

abstract.en: See a hand stroking a rough chin.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手抚过粗糙的下巴。

abstract.en: See a man walking straight toward danger.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人径直走向危险。

examples.en: The old man stroked his grey beard.
examples.cn: 老人捋了捋花白的胡须。

examples.en: He decided to grow a beard.
examples.cn: 他决定留胡子。

examples.en: He bearded the lion in its den.
examples.cn: 他闯入狮穴公然挑衅。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 beard 想成垂在下巴上的一把刷子。

root: 源自拉丁语 barba「胡须」，经古法语 barbe 进入中古英语写作 berd，后定型为 beard；动词义由「抓住狮子的胡须」引申为公然对抗。

sensesIntro.en: Facial hair and a bold challenge share one word.
sensesIntro.cn: 面部毛发与大胆挑衅，共用一个词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a grey beard falling to the chest.
core.cn: 核心意象：垂到胸前的花白络腮胡。

branches.en: a long beard
branches.cn: 长胡须

branches.en: grow a beard
branches.cn: 留胡子

branches.en: a full beard
branches.cn: 络腮胡

branches.en: beard the lion
branches.cn: 捋虎须

branches.en: beard a rival
branches.cn: 公然对抗对手

intro.en: Beard takes -s, -ed and -less endings.
intro.cn: beard 可加 -s、-ed、-less 后缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is barba, a beard.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基是 barba，意为「胡须」。

definition_zh: 标签；标记；称号；贴标签；把……称为
definition_en: a small piece of paper or cloth giving information about something, a word used to describe a person or group, or to fix such a tag on something
core_image: 一只玻璃罐上贴着一方白纸，写着内容与日期
scene: 厨房的架子上摆满一排玻璃罐，里面装着不同颜色的粉。 She wrote the date on a label and stuck it to the jar of flour.
sceneCN: 这里 label 是「标签」（第 1 个义项：提供信息的小纸片或布片），句意是她在标签上写了日期，贴在面粉罐上。画面里有厨房架子、一排玻璃罐与一方白纸。

derivatives.zh: 加 -ed 构成，义为「贴有标签的；被称作的」
加 -ing 构成，义为「贴标签；标签说明」
植物学术语，由本词派生，义为「有唇瓣的」

senses.title: A tag giving information
senses.definition: a small piece of paper, cloth, or plastic fixed to an object to show what it is, who made it, or what it contains
senses.definitionCN: 贴在物件上、说明其名称、制作者或成分的小纸片、布片或塑片
senses.example: The washing label says to use cold water.
senses.exampleCN: 洗标上写着要用冷水洗。
senses.why: The core object is a small carrier of written information attached to something bigger.
senses.whyCN: 核心物件是一小块信息的载体，附着在更大的物体上。

senses.title: A word used to classify someone
senses.definition: a short word or phrase used to describe a person, a group, or a style, often too simply
senses.definitionCN: 用来描述某人、某群体或某种风格的简短词语，常失之简单
senses.example: She dislikes the label of a protest singer.
senses.exampleCN: 她不喜欢「抗议歌手」这个标签。
senses.why: Once the written tag is put on an object, the same gesture is done to people with a word, and the metaphor is fixed.
senses.whyCN: 文字标签既可贴物，同样的动作也可以用词贴人，这个比喻便固定下来。

senses.title: To fix a tag on something
senses.definition: to attach a label to an object, or to write information on it
senses.definitionCN: 给物件贴标签，或在上面写明信息
senses.example: All the boxes must be labelled before shipping.
senses.exampleCN: 所有箱子在发运前都必须贴好标签。
senses.why: The noun of a tag becomes the verb of attaching one, as English commonly does with objects.
senses.whyCN: 标签这一物件名词转为「贴上标签」的动词，英语中这类器物转动词很常见。

senses.title: To describe or brand
senses.definition: to describe a person or thing with a particular word, often unfairly
senses.definitionCN: 用某个词描述某人或某物，常带不公意味
senses.example: The paper labelled the plan a waste of money.
senses.exampleCN: 报纸把这项计划称作浪费钱。
senses.why: The verb repeats on people what the noun does to jars: a word is stuck on and then treated as the truth.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词对罐子所做的事用到人身上：把一个词贴上去，随后当作事实。

senses.title: A brand name on goods
senses.definition: the name of a company or designer shown on a product, especially in fashion
senses.definitionCN: 商品上显示的公司或设计师名称，尤见于时装
senses.example: He refuses to pay extra for a designer label.
senses.exampleCN: 他拒绝为名牌标识多付钱。
senses.why: In fashion the maker name became the thing itself, so a label on the collar can double the price.
senses.whyCN: 在时装业里制作者之名成了东西本身，于是领口上一个标签就能让价格翻倍。

intro.en: Label comes from an Old French word for a rag or ribbon, and its meaning moved from the strip to the information written on it.
intro.cn: label 源自古法语中表示「布条、丝带」的词，词义由那条带子转到写在带子上的信息。

items.en: A Germanic root meaning to hang down or to flap lies behind the French word.
items.cn: 法语这个词的背后，是一个表示「垂下、飘动」的日耳曼语词根。

items.en: Label meant a narrow strip or ribbon hanging loose, often attached to a seal or a garment.
items.cn: label 指垂着的一条窄带或丝带，常系在印章或衣物上。

items.en: English borrowed it for the paper strip that carried a name or an address.
items.cn: 英语借它指写着名字或地址的纸条。

items.en: The strip and its writing merged, so label came to mean the written information itself.
items.cn: 带子与上面的文字合为一体，label 遂指文字信息本身。

items.en: The word turns into a metaphor and a verb: people are labelled, and brands are labels.
items.cn: 这个词转为比喻与动词：人被贴标签，品牌也被称作 label。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers derived forms and close spellings; the near-meaning group gathers other words for tags and names.
note.cn: 形近组收派生形式与相近拼写；近义组收其他表示标签与名称的词。

entries.definition: The past form and adjective, spelled with one l in American English.
entries.definitionCN: 过去式与形容词，美式英语只写一个 l。

entries.definition: A common wrong spelling, with the two letters swapped.
entries.definitionCN: 常见错拼，两个字母颠倒了。

entries.definition: One letter away, and it means a published false statement that harms someone.
entries.definitionCN: 只差一个字母，指发表出来损害他人的不实之词。

entries.definition: A small movable card or plastic piece attached to show price or owner.
entries.definitionCN: 附于物件、显示价格或主人的可移动小牌。

entries.definition: A gummed piece of paper stuck on a surface.
entries.definitionCN: 贴在表面的带胶纸片。

entries.definition: The name of a product or company, or a mark made by burning.
entries.definitionCN: 产品或公司的名称，也可指烙印。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the rag origin of the word, the British and American spellings, and the phrases it appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用这个词「布条」的来源、英美两种拼写，以及常见搭配。

normal.en: Label once meant a hanging strip of cloth, and now it means what is written on it.
normal.cn: label 原是垂着的一条布，如今指写在布上的字。

normal.en: British English doubles the l: labelled, labelling.
normal.cn: 英式英语双写 l：labelled、labelling。

normal.en: Read the label before you wash the shirt.
normal.cn: 洗衬衫之前先看标签。

normal.en: To label someone is to stick a word on them and walk away.
normal.cn: 给某人贴标签，就是把一个词贴在他身上然后走开。

normal.en: A designer label costs more for the name than for the cloth.
normal.cn: 名牌标识贵的是名字，而非布料。

abstract.en: A label is a promise of order: one small paper, and a whole shelf becomes readable.
abstract.cn: 标签是秩序的一份承诺：一小片纸，整排架子便读得懂。

abstract.en: The same act that helps a jar be found can make a person be misunderstood.
abstract.cn: 帮人找到罐子的同一动作，也能让人被误解。

abstract.en: What is written on the outside is not the thing inside, a difference worth keeping in mind whenever a label is read.
abstract.cn: 外面写的并非里面之物，每次看标签时都值得记住这个差别。

examples.en: Check the label for the ingredients.
examples.cn: 查看标签上的成分表。

examples.en: Every file was labelled with a date.
examples.cn: 每个文件都标上了日期。

examples.en: It is unfair to label him a trouble-maker.
examples.cn: 称他为麻烦制造者是不公平的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「累抱」——抱着罐子累了一路，就为看清那方标签

root: 古法语 label「垂着的布条、丝带」，背后是表示「垂下」的日耳曼语词根；中古英语借入指写有姓名地址的纸条，后由带子转为上面所写的信息，并引申出「称号」与「贴标签、把……称为」等义。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: the information tag, the word used of a person, the act of tagging, the act of branding someone with a word, and the brand name on goods.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：信息标签，用于人的称号，贴标签的动作，用词给人定性，以及商品上的品牌标识。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a square of white paper on a jar, with a name and a date in ink.
core.cn: 核心意象：玻璃罐上一方白纸，墨写着名称与日期。

branches.en: THE TAG LINE: a small carrier of written information attached to a thing.
branches.cn: 标签线：附着在物件上、承载文字信息的小片。

branches.en: THE WORD LINE: a short word stuck on a person, a style or a garment.
branches.cn: 词语线：贴在人、风格或衣物上的简短说法。

branches.en: THE ACTION LINE: the verb fixes a tag on an object.
branches.cn: 动作线：动词给物件贴上标签。

branches.en: THE JUDGEMENT LINE: the same act with words can be unfair.
branches.cn: 判断线：用词做同样的事，可能不公。

branches.en: THE FORM LINE: object and action share one form, as English often allows.
branches.cn: 形式线：物件与动作共用一个形式，英语常这样。

intro.en: Label is a French loan whose family grows through spelling variants and ordinary suffixes.
intro.cn: label 是法语借词，其词族靠拼写变体与普通后缀扩展。

latinIntro.en: Label is not Latin in origin, though the French form goes back to a Germanic strip.
latinIntro.cn: label 并非源自拉丁语，其法语形式可上溯到日耳曼语中「布条」一词。

definition_zh: 祷告；祈祷；祷文；祈祷者；祈盼
definition_en: the act of speaking to a god, the words used for it, a person who prays, and the thing that is earnestly hoped for
core_image: 合十的双手上方，一段固定的话被反复念到能背
scene: 手术室外的走廊很安静，母亲把手提包放在膝上，闭上眼默默念了一句。 She said a silent prayer and looked up at the closed door.
sceneCN: 这里是「祷告、祈祷」（第 1 个义项：向神说话的行为）；句意为她默默做了一次祷告，抬头望向关着的门。图中可辨识物件：长椅、手提包、关着的门。

pos.zh: 祷告；祈祷；祷文；祈祷者；祈盼

derivatives.zh: 由 prayer 加 -ful 构成，义为「虔诚祈祷的；常祷告的」
prayerful 加 -ly 构成，义为「虔诚地祈祷着」
prayerful 加 -ness 构成，义为「虔诚祈祷的状态」

senses.title: The act of speaking to a god
senses.definition: the act of speaking to a god, silently or aloud, in order to worship, give thanks or ask for something
senses.definitionCN: 向神说话的行为，可以默念也可以出声，用以敬拜、感恩或求助
senses.example: Her morning prayer takes about ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 她早晨的祷告大约要十分钟。
senses.why: The noun is the verb pray with a French-shaped ending, so its first job is simply to give the activity a name.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词是在动词 pray 后面接上一个法语式的词尾构成的，所以它最基本的作用就是把动词所描述的活动变成一个名字。

senses.title: The words used in praying
senses.definition: a fixed or composed set of words spoken or read when praying
senses.definitionCN: 祈祷时说出或读出的固定文本，或临时组织的一段话
senses.example: The children learned the Lord's Prayer by heart.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们把《主祷文》背了下来。
senses.why: Once the activity has a name, the words that carry it can be named too, so a prayer becomes a text that can be learned, printed and repeated.
senses.whyCN: 活动有了名字之后，承载这场活动的那些话也就可以被命名，于是 prayer 成为可以背诵、印刷、反复念的文本。

senses.title: A person who prays
senses.definition: someone who prays, formed as pray plus -er and pronounced with two syllables
senses.definitionCN: 做祈祷的人，由 pray 加 -er 构成，读作两个音节
senses.example: A faithful prayer, she attends the dawn service every day.
senses.exampleCN: 她是个虔诚的祈祷者，每天都参加清晨的礼拜。
senses.why: English often adds -er to a verb to name the doer, so pray plus -er gives a person; that spelling is said pray-er, while the noun for the act has lost its second syllable.
senses.whyCN: 英语常给动词加 -er 来表示「做这件事的人」，pray 加 -er 便指祈祷的人；这个写法读作 pray-er，而表示行为的名词已经把第二个音节省掉了。

senses.title: An earnest hope or request
senses.definition: something strongly hoped for, often spoken of as if it were a request made to fate
senses.definitionCN: 殷切盼望的事，常被说成仿佛是对命运提出的请求
senses.example: It is my prayer that the two sides will talk again.
senses.exampleCN: 我祈盼双方能够再次坐下来谈。
senses.why: If a prayer is a request, then the thing requested can take the same name, which is why the word can mean the wish itself rather than the words or the act.
senses.whyCN: 既然祷告是一种请求，被请求的那件事也可以沿用同一个词，于是 prayer 能指愿望本身，而不只是话语或行为。

senses.title: A brief spoken request at a meal or ceremony
senses.definition: a short blessing said before a meal or at the start of a ceremony
senses.definitionCN: 饭前或仪式开始时说的简短祝祷词
senses.example: The grandfather said a quick prayer over the food.
senses.exampleCN: 祖父在饭食前迅速做了一段祝祷。
senses.why: A prayer is the act in the smallest unit: one short text, one moment.
senses.whyCN: 祷告的最小单位就是一次短促的行为：一段短短的话，一个时刻。

senses.title: A regular time of prayer in a community
senses.definition: an appointed time or office of prayer in a religious community
senses.definitionCN: 宗教团体中规定的祷告时辰或功课
senses.example: Bells rang for evening prayer across the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 晚祷的钟声响彻山谷。
senses.why: Communities turn the act into a schedule, and the scheduled act keeps the same name.
senses.whyCN: 团体把行为排入时刻表，排定时段的行为沿用同一个名字。

senses.title: A mere chance or hope, faint as a prayer
senses.definition: a very slight chance or hope, said as faint as a prayer
senses.definitionCN: 极渺茫的机会或希望，常说 a prayer（渺茫如一次祷告）
senses.example: Without new evidence, the appeal did not have a prayer.
senses.exampleCN: 没有新证据，这场上诉毫无指望。
senses.why: A request that may go unanswered measures the smallest of hopes, so the word becomes the unit of faint chance.
senses.whyCN: 可能不被应允的请求衡量着最小的希望，这个词于是成了渺茫机会的计量单位。

senses.title: The verbal part of a service
senses.definition: the section of a religious service devoted to spoken prayer
senses.definitionCN: 礼拜仪式中专用于祷告的环节
senses.example: The choir fell silent during the prayer.
senses.exampleCN: 祷告环节时，唱诗班安静下来。
senses.why: Within a liturgy each act has its slot, and the act's name labels the slot.
senses.whyCN: 在礼拜仪式中每个行为都有其时段，行为的名字便成了时段的标签。

intro.en: The noun grew out of the Latin verb of entreaty, took its shape in French, and split in pronunciation from the person who prays.
intro.cn: 这个名词从拉丁语中表示恳求的动词长出来，在法语里定型，后来读音又与「祈祷的人」分了家。

items.en: The verb precari meant to entreat or beg, and it stands behind both the verb pray and the noun prayer.
items.cn: 动词 precari 意为恳求、乞求，pray 与 prayer 两个词都源于它。

items.en: A noun use of the same stem, precaria meant entreaty or the things one begs for, and it supplied the shape of the later noun.
items.cn: 同一词干的名词用法 precaria 指恳求或所乞求之物，为后来的名词提供了形态基础。

items.en: Old French preiere meant a prayer or an entreaty and was the form English borrowed for the noun.
items.cn: 古法语 preiere 意为祈祷、恳求，英语借的正是这个名词形式。

items.en: Middle English used prayer for both the act and the words, and the spelling settled without the final -e of the French form.
items.cn: 中古英语用 prayer 兼指祈祷的行为和祷词，拼写定型时去掉了法语词尾的 -e。

items.en: Modern English says the noun for the act as /preə/, while the person who prays keeps a fuller pray-er sound; the two uses drifted apart in speech.
items.cn: 现代英语把指行为的名词读作 /preə/，而「祈祷的人」保留了更完整的 pray-er 读音；两种用法在口语里逐渐分开。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the verb and the family built around it; the near-meaning group gathers words for devotion and for urgent asking.
note.cn: 形近组收动词本身及其词族；近义组收表示虔诚、敬拜或急切请求的词。

entries.definition: The verb that prayer is built on, meaning to speak to a god or to beg.
entries.definitionCN: prayer 所由构成的动词，意为祈祷或恳求。

entries.definition: Given to prayer; showing devotion.
entries.definitionCN: 常做祷告的；虔诚的。

entries.definition: An animal hunted for food by another animal.
entries.definitionCN: 猎物；被捕食的动物。只是读音相同、拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Too eager to know about other people's private affairs.
entries.definitionCN: 爱打听别人私事的。只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Deep love and loyalty shown to a god or to a person.
entries.definitionCN: 对神或对人的深切爱戴与忠诚；虔诚。

entries.definition: A humble and urgent request made to someone in power.
entries.definitionCN: 向掌权者低声而急切地提出的请求；恳求。

entries.definition: The activity of showing reverence to a god, often in a service.
entries.definitionCN: 对神的敬拜，常在仪式中进行。

entries.definition: An emotional request made when someone is in trouble.
entries.definitionCN: 身处困境时提出的恳切请求。

normalIntro.en: The noun is the verb plus an ending, and the endings it carries keep pointing back to the act of praying.
normalIntro.cn: 这个名词就是动词加一个词尾，而它携带的词尾始终指向「祈祷」这个动作。

normal.en: The noun is the verb plus an ending, so anything the verb can do, the noun can name as an activity.
normal.cn: 这个名词就是动词加一个词尾，因此动词能做的事，名词都能把它当作一种活动来命名。

normal.en: The second syllable vanished: what was pray-er for the act became prayer, while the person kept a clearer pray-er sound.
normal.cn: 第二个音节消失了：指行为的 pray-er 变成 prayer，而指人的说法则保留了更清楚的 pray-er 读音。

normal.en: Say a prayer: the verb say shows that a prayer can be a piece of language, not only a feeling.
normal.cn: say a prayer 这个搭配里的 say 说明 prayer 可以是一段话语，而不只是一种心情。

normal.en: The Lord's Prayer is a fixed text, a clear example of prayer as words rather than as an act.
normal.cn: 《主祷文》是一段固定文本，清楚展示了 prayer 作为「话语」而非「行为」的用法。

normal.en: Prayer book and prayer meeting keep the noun in compounds, where the first element names the purpose.
normal.cn: prayer book 和 prayer meeting 把这个名词留在复合词里，前一部分说明用途。

abstract.en: A prayer is the shape a wish takes when it is spoken to someone who may not answer.
abstract.cn: 祷告是一个愿望在被说给未必回应的人听时所采取的形态。

abstract.en: The same letters cover an act, a text and a person, and only the voice tells them apart.
abstract.cn: 同样几个字母同时指行为、文本和人，只有读音把它们区分开。

abstract.en: People rarely pray calmly; the word is loudest when nothing else can be done.
abstract.cn: 人很少心平气和地祷告；当别的办法都没有时，这个词最响。

examples.en: Saying a prayer before meals is a habit in her family.
examples.cn: 饭前祷告是她家的习惯。

examples.en: The letter read like a prayer for forgiveness.
examples.cn: 那封信读起来像一篇祈求宽恕的祷文。

examples.en: His prayer was that the ship would reach the shore.
examples.cn: 他祈盼船能靠岸。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普瑞尔」——声音软下来，像是把话轻轻说给天上听；prayer 就是祷告。

root: 拉丁语 precari（恳求）的名词形式 precaria 经古法语 preiere 进入英语；与动词 pray 同源，但读音走了两条路。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the act of praying; from it come the words used, the person who prays, and the wish that is prayed for.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「祈祷」这一行为；由它分出所用的祷词、做祈祷的人，以及被祈求的那个愿望。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands joined above a page of fixed words, repeated until they are known by heart.
core.cn: 核心意象：合十的双手悬在一页固定文字之上，反复念到能背下来。

branches.en: a woman closing her eyes at the side of a hospital corridor
branches.cn: 医院走廊边闭眼的女人

branches.en: a child reciting a text learned by heart
branches.cn: 背诵一段熟记文字的孩子

branches.en: an old worshipper kneeling longer than the others
branches.cn: 跪得比别人久的老人

branches.en: a sentence written at the end of a letter, asking fate for a favour
branches.cn: 信末写下的那句话，向命运讨一个人情

branches.en: the same words passed from one pair of hands to the next
branches.cn: 同样的话语从一双手传到另一双手

intro.en: The noun is the Latin verb of entreaty reshaped by a Latin noun ending and then by French, with English suffixes growing from the result.
intro.cn: 这个名词由拉丁语中表示恳求的动词，经拉丁名词词尾和法语先后改写而成，再由英语后缀长出新的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies both the verb of entreaty and the noun built on it; French then trimmed the word into the shape English borrowed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语既提供了表示恳求的动词，也提供了由它构成的名词；法语随后把它修剪成英语借用的形状。

items.meaningCN: 构成表示状态或结果的名词

definition_zh: 数量；数额；总额；金额；达到（某数量）；等同于
definition_en: a quantity of something, especially money, or the total reached when things are added up; as a verb, to add up to or be equivalent to
core_image: 一堆东西越堆越高，数字沿着刻度一路往上爬
scene: 集市收摊时，摊主把零钱一张张摊在木板上清点。 The amount in the tin was just enough to pay for the week's rent.
sceneCN: 这里 amount 是「数额、总数」（第 1 个义项：某物的数量或总和）；句意为铁盒里的钱刚好够付一周的房租。画面里有收摊的木板、摊开的零钱与清点的摊主。

pos.zh: 名词：数量；数额；总额；金额
动词：合计达；等同于；意味着

derivatives.zh: 由本词加介词 to 构成的动词短语，义为「合计达；等同于」
由本词加介词短语构成的正式说法，义为「合计达……之多」，多用于法律与财务文本

senses.title: A quantity of something
senses.definition: how much of something there is, especially when it is uncountable or measured in bulk
senses.definitionCN: 某物有多少，尤指不可数或以整体计量的东西
senses.example: A large amount of rain fell in a single night.
senses.exampleCN: 一夜之间下了大量的雨。
senses.why: The Old French verb meant to go up: as goods are piled or counted, the total climbs, and the climbed total is the amount.
senses.whyCN: 古法语动词意为「向上走」：东西越堆越多、越数越多，总数随之上爬，爬到的那个总数就是 amount。

senses.title: The total of several things
senses.definition: the sum reached when several quantities or costs are added together
senses.definitionCN: 把若干数量或费用相加之后得到的和
senses.example: The final amount on the bill surprised everyone at the table.
senses.exampleCN: 账单上的最终总额让桌旁所有人都吃了一惊。
senses.why: Adding is a way of going up, so the completed addition is named by the same upward movement.
senses.whyCN: 相加就是一种「往上走」，所以加法做完的结果也用同一个「上升」的动作来命名。

senses.title: A sum of money to be paid
senses.definition: a particular sum of money, especially one written on a bill, cheque or account
senses.definitionCN: 特定的一笔钱，尤指写在账单、支票或账户上的数目
senses.example: Please write the amount in words as well as in figures.
senses.exampleCN: 请同时用文字和数字写出金额。
senses.why: Money is the most common thing that gets counted up, so the general total narrows into the figure on a payment.
senses.whyCN: 钱是最常被累加的东西，于是笼统的「总数」收窄成付款单上的那个数字。

senses.title: To add up to a figure
senses.definition: to reach a particular total when everything is counted or added
senses.definitionCN: 把所有项目计入或相加后达到某个总数
senses.example: The repairs amounted to more than the car was worth.
senses.exampleCN: 维修费合计起来超过了这辆车本身的价值。
senses.why: The verb turns the noun into motion: the figures climb until they arrive at a total.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词变成运动：数字一路攀升，直到抵达某个总数。

senses.title: To be equivalent to something
senses.definition: to be equal in effect or meaning to something else, often something unstated
senses.definitionCN: 在效果或含义上等同于另一件事，常指未明说的事
senses.example: His silence amounted to an admission of guilt.
senses.exampleCN: 他的沉默等于承认了过错。
senses.why: If counted together, the facts add up to one conclusion; the total is not money but meaning.
senses.whyCN: 把事实合起来一算，会得出同一个结论；此时的总数不是钱，而是含义。

intro.en: Amount comes from a Latin phrase about climbing a hill, which French turned into a verb of rising totals.
intro.cn: amount 源自一个关于「上山」的拉丁短语，法语把它变成了表示「总数上升」的动词。

items.en: The phrase ad montem meant 'to the mountain, upward', from ad 'to' and mons, montem 'mountain'.
items.cn: 短语 ad montem 意为「向山、向上」，由 ad「向」与 mons、montem「山」构成。

items.en: The phrase contracted into amont, an adverb meaning 'above, upward'.
items.cn: 这个短语缩合成副词 amont，意为「在上方、向上」。

items.en: The verb amonter meant 'to go up, to rise', and in accounts 'to amount to'.
items.cn: 动词 amonter 意为「上升、升高」，在账目语境中意为「合计达」。

items.en: English borrowed the verb and formed the noun amount, first meaning the total that something rises to.
items.cn: 英语借入这个动词，并造出名词 amount，最初指某物累加后达到的总数。

items.en: The money sense became dominant, and the verb specialized into the phrase amount to.
items.cn: 与钱有关的义项成为主流，动词则主要固定在短语 amount to 里。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin image of a mountain; the near-meaning group gathers words for quantities and totals.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「山」的意象；近义组收表示数量与总数的词。

entries.definition: To climb up or increase; also a mountain, from the same Latin source.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「登上、增加」，也可作名词指山，与 amount 同出拉丁语「山」的意象。

entries.definition: A very high hill; from Latin montem, the same word inside the phrase behind amount.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「山」，来自拉丁语 montem，正是 amount 背后那个短语里的词。

entries.definition: Of the highest importance; its second element comes from Old French amont, upward.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「至高无上的、最重要的」，后半部分来自古法语 amont「向上」。

entries.definition: A measurable amount of something, often used in technical or formal contexts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「数量」，指可测量的量，多用于技术或正式语境。

entries.definition: The total of numbers added together, or a quantity of money.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「总数、金额」，指若干数字相加的结果或一笔钱。

entries.definition: The complete figure after everything has been counted.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「总数、合计」，指全部计入后的完整数字。

entries.definition: A count of items, usually countable things rather than bulk material.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「数目」，通常指数得清的物件，而不是成堆的材料。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the real Latin hill image, its French descendants, and the money frame the word lives in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子沿着真实的拉丁语「山」意象、它的法语后代，以及这个词所处的金钱语境展开。

normal.en: Ad montem is to the mountain: a total is something you climb up to.
normal.cn: ad montem 是「向山去」：总数就是一路爬上去到达的地方。

normal.en: Amont is upward in Old French, and amonter is to rise; amount keeps that upward motion.
normal.cn: 古法语 amont 是「向上」，amonter 是「上升」，amount 保留了这个向上的动作。

normal.en: Mountain and mount are close relatives from the same Latin word for a hill.
normal.cn: mountain 与 mount 是同族近亲，都来自同一个表示「山」的拉丁词。

normal.en: Amount to is the verb frame: costs amount to a total, facts amount to a conclusion.
normal.cn: amount to 是动词句式：费用合计成一个总数，事实合起来等于一个结论。

normal.en: A bill always shows an amount, which is why the money sense dominates today.
normal.cn: 账单上总有一个 amount，这就是今天与钱有关的义项占主流的原因。

abstract.en: Picture a pile of coins growing taller and taller until it reaches a marked line on the wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一堆硬币越堆越高，直到碰到墙上划好的一道线。

abstract.en: Picture a staircase of numbers, each step a receipt, the top landing the final total.
abstract.cn: 想象一道由数字组成的楼梯，每一级是一张收据，最上面的平台就是最终总额。

abstract.en: Picture a heap of small facts that suddenly tips over into one clear conclusion.
abstract.cn: 想象一堆零散事实忽然倾倒，落成一个清楚的结论。

examples.en: The amount in the tin was just enough to pay for the week's rent.
examples.cn: 铁盒里的钱刚好够付一周的房租。

examples.en: A large amount of rain fell in a single night.
examples.cn: 一夜之间下了大量的雨。

examples.en: His silence amounted to an admission of guilt.
examples.cn: 他的沉默等于承认了过错。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿蒙特」——阿蒙把钱堆成小山，越高越接近总数：数量、总额

root: 拉丁语短语 ad montem「向山、向上」由 ad「向」+ mons、montem「山」构成，缩合为古法语副词 amont「向上」，再派生动词 amonter「上升、合计达」。英语借入动词并造出名词 amount，先指累加达到的总数，后以金额义为主。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses all follow one rising line: a quantity, the completed total, the money figure, the verb of reaching a total, and the moment when facts add up to a meaning.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项都沿着同一条上升线：一个数量、加完后的总数、钱上的数字、达到总数的动词，以及事实合起来等于某个含义的那一刻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pile rises toward a marked line, and the line it reaches is the amount.
core.cn: 核心意象：一堆东西朝一道刻度线升高，达到那道线时就是 amount。

branches.en: THE QUANTITY LINE: the bulk itself, before any addition is finished.
branches.cn: 数量线：加法还没做完时，那一堆东西本身的量。

branches.en: THE TOTAL LINE: addition completed, the figure at the top of the climb.
branches.cn: 总数线：加法做完，爬升到顶端的那个数字。

branches.en: THE MONEY LINE: the most countable thing, narrowed to a sum on a bill.
branches.cn: 金额线：最常被累加的钱，收窄成账单上的一个数字。

branches.en: THE VERB LINE: the figures themselves climb to a total.
branches.cn: 动词线：数字自己一路攀升，达到一个总数。

branches.en: THE MEANING LINE: facts added together reach a conclusion rather than a sum of money.
branches.cn: 含义线：事实合起来抵达的是一个结论，而不是一笔钱。

intro.en: Amount is a Latin prepositional phrase that became a French adverb and verb, then an English noun; its parts are not suffixes but direction words.
intro.cn: amount 是一个拉丁介词短语，先变成法语副词与动词，再成为英语名词；它的组成部分不是后缀，而是表示方向的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin ad and mons are recorded words, and the French forms are documented; nothing here is a reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ad 与 mons 都是有记录的词，法语形式也有文献可查，这里没有重构形式。

items.example: It appears in montem and in mountain.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 montem 与 mountain 中。

items.example: The phrase became this single adverb.
items.exampleCN: 那个短语变成了这个单一副词。

items.meaningCN: 复数或第三人称单数形式
