definition_zh: 失业的；未被雇用的；未被利用的
definition_en: not having a paid job, or not being used
core_image: 工牌摘下后空着的手，和一张没排上日程的椅子
scene: 工厂大门贴出了歇业通知，人们攥着最后一个月的工资条站在门口。 Thousands of workers were left unemployed when the factory closed.
sceneCN: 这里 unemployed 是形容词「失业的」（第 1 个义项：失去有薪工作）；句意为工厂关闭后数千名工人失业。

pos.zh: 失业的；未被雇用的；未被利用的

derivatives.zh: 由本词变 -ed 为 -ment 构成，义为「失业；失业率；失业状态」
去掉否定前缀后的词基，义为「雇用；使用」
由词基加施动者后缀构成，义为「雇主」
由词基加后缀构成，义为「雇员」

senses.title: Without a paid job
senses.definition: not having a job that pays wages or a salary, though able and often willing to work
senses.definitionCN: 没有领取工资或薪金的工作，但有工作能力且通常愿意工作
senses.example: He was unemployed for six months before finding a new post.
senses.exampleCN: 他失业了六个月才找到新职位。
senses.why: The prefix un- turns employ into its opposite: the hand that once held the tool now holds nothing.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 un- 把 employ 翻转为反面：曾经握着工具的手如今空无一物。

senses.title: Temporarily out of work
senses.definition: out of work between jobs, often for a limited period
senses.definitionCN: 处于两份工作之间的待业状态，常为有限时段
senses.example: After graduation she was unemployed for only a few weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 毕业后她只待业了几个星期。
senses.why: Being unemployed is a state, not a character trait: the un- marks a temporary vacancy, not a permanent lack.
senses.whyCN: 失业是一种状态而非本性：un- 标记的是暂时的空缺，而非永久的匮乏。

senses.title: Not being used
senses.definition: not currently being put to use, said of machines, capital, or resources
senses.definitionCN: 未被投入使用，用于机器、资金或资源
senses.example: A large part of the fund sat unemployed in a low-interest account.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔资金的大部分闲置在一个低息账户里。
senses.why: Employ once meant simply to use; anything can be employed, so anything can be unemployed — hands, money, machines.
senses.whyCN: employ 本义只是「使用」；任何东西都可被使用，因此任何东西都可能未被使用——手、资金、机器皆然。

senses.title: Skill or effort left idle
senses.titleCN: 才能或精力未被施展的
senses.definition: not given an outlet or occupation, said of abilities or energy
senses.definitionCN: 才能或精力没有得到施展的用武之地
senses.example: His talent sat unemployed in the small branch office.
senses.exampleCN: 他的才华在小小的分部里无处施展。
senses.why: A skill unexercised is like a tool unemployed: both wait for the hand that will put them back to work.
senses.whyCN: 未被施展的才能如同闲置的工具：二者都在等待那只把它们重新用起来的手。

senses.title: Registered as job-seeking
senses.definition: officially recorded as out of work and seeking employment, as in labour statistics
senses.definitionCN: 在劳动统计中被正式记录为无工作且正在求职
senses.example: She registered as unemployed at the local job centre.
senses.exampleCN: 她在当地就业服务中心登记为失业。
senses.why: The state needs the word to draw a line: not employed, not retired, but actively looking.
senses.whyCN: 统计制度需要这个词划出一条界线：既非在职、也非退休，而是正在积极求职。

senses.title: The unemployed as a group
senses.definition: the unemployed, as a collective noun for all people without work
senses.definitionCN: the unemployed 作集合名词，指所有没有工作的人
senses.example: The marchers included many of the long-term unemployed.
senses.exampleCN: 游行队伍中有许多长期失业者。
senses.why: The adjective stiffens into a noun: the whole class of people defined by the absence of employment.
senses.whyCN: 形容词凝固成名词：整个群体被「没有工作」这一缺席所定义。

senses.title: Seasonal or cyclical idleness
senses.titleCN: 季节性或周期性失业的
senses.definition: out of work because of the season or a business cycle, as in seasonal trades
senses.definitionCN: 因季节或经济周期而无工作，见于季节性行业
senses.example: Dockworkers were seasonally unemployed each winter.
senses.exampleCN: 码头工人每年冬天都会季节性失业。
senses.why: The tide of work goes out and comes back; un-employed names the low water of employment.
senses.whyCN: 工作的潮水会退去也会回来；un-employed 命名的正是雇用潮的低水位。

senses.title: Idle hours or facilities
senses.definition: of time, rooms, or equipment lying unused, as in unemployed hours
senses.definitionCN: 指时间、房间或设备处于闲置状态，如 unemployed hours
senses.example: The unemployed evenings of that winter were filled with chess.
senses.exampleCN: 那年冬天闲置的夜晚都用来下棋。
senses.why: Even time can be employed or unemployed: hours with no occupation stretch like empty factory halls.
senses.whyCN: 连时间也可被「使用」或「闲置」：无所事事的钟点像空置的厂房一样漫长。

intro.en: Unemployed is employ wrapped in the Old English negative un-, with a French body and a Germanic shell.
intro.cn: unemployed 是 employ 加上古英语否定前缀 un-：法语的身躯，日耳曼的外壳。

items.en: Latin implicare meant to enfold or entangle; its participle implicitus and variant implicatus fed the sense of being held or busy.
items.cn: 拉丁语 implicare 意为「包住；缠住」，其分词 implicitus 与变体 implicatus 衍生出「被占用；忙碌」之义。

items.en: Old French employer meant to use, apply, or engage; the Latin root had shifted from entangling to making use of.
items.cn: 古法语 employer 意为「使用；应用；聘用」，拉丁词根由「缠绕」转为「利用」。

items.en: The verb is recorded from the fifteenth century, first for using things and then for hiring people.
items.cn: 动词约自十五世纪有记录，先用于「使用物」，后用于「雇用人」。

items.en: The prefix un-, from Old English un-, attaches negatives to adjectives and participles; it is cognate with Latin in- and Greek a(n)-.
items.cn: 前缀 un- 来自古英语，加在形容词与分词前构成否定；它与拉丁语 in-、希腊语 a(n)- 同源。

items.en: The participle unemployed is recorded from the late sixteenth century, at first also for unused things.
items.cn: 分词 unemployed 约自十六世纪末有记录，最初也可指「未被使用之物」。

items.en: Unemployment followed as the abstract noun, and the pair now anchors the vocabulary of labour statistics.
items.cn: 抽象名词 unemployment 随之出现，这对词如今是劳动统计词汇的基石。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the employ family and un- counterparts; the near-meaning group gathers words for being without work.
note.cn: 形近组收 employ 词族与 un- 对应词；近义组收「没有工作」类词。

entries.definition: The abstract noun for the state of being unemployed.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「失业；失业率；失业状态」。

entries.definition: The positive participle: having a job.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「受雇的；有工作的」，为本词的正面形式。

entries.definition: The person hired; the ee- receives the action.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「雇员」，后缀 -ee 表示动作的接受方。

entries.definition: The person or company that hires; the er- gives the action.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「雇主」，后缀 -er 表示动作的发出方。

entries.definition: To put into position; shares the Old French ending but not the Latin root, only similar in sound.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「部署；调配」，与 employ 词根不同只是拼写相近，词源无关。

entries.definition: Without a job; more informal and direct.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无工作的」，语气更口语、更直接。

entries.definition: A phrase with the same meaning, common in everyday speech.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「失业的」，日常口语常用。

entries.definition: Not working or in use; broader, covering machines and time as well.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「闲置的；空闲的」，适用面更广，也指机器与时间。

entries.definition: Losing a job because the post itself is no longer needed, chiefly British.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「（因岗位撤销而）被裁员的」，多用于英式英语。

entries.definition: The verb for ending someone's employment for economic reasons.
entries.definitionCN: 短语动词，义为「裁员；暂时解雇」，强调因经济原因终止雇用。

normalIntro.en: Five anchors from the prefix, the root, and the family.
normalIntro.cn: 五个来自前缀、词根与词族的记忆锚点。

normal.en: Un- plus employed: the employed hand is full, the unemployed hand is empty.
normal.cn: un- 加 employed：受雇的手是满的，失业的手是空的。

normal.en: Employ is French-faced but means simply to use: hands, people, money.
normal.cn: employ 面孔像法语词，但本义只是「使用」：用手、用人、用钱。

normal.en: Employee receives the job (-ee), employer gives it (-er).
normal.cn: employee 接收工作（-ee），employer 发出工作（-er）。

normal.en: Unemployment is the state; unemployed is the person in that state.
normal.cn: unemployment 是状态，unemployed 是处于该状态的人。

normal.en: Deploy looks like employ but only deploys, it does not hire.
normal.cn: deploy 拼写像 employ，但只「部署」，不「雇用」。

abstract.en: Picture an empty badge hook beside a full one on the factory wall.
abstract.cn: 想象工厂墙上，一个空着的工牌挂钩旁边是一个满着的挂钩。

abstract.en: Un- is a hand that unclenches: what was held falls away.
abstract.cn: un- 是一只松开的手：原本握住的东西就此脱落。

abstract.en: Being unemployed is a pause between two beats of work, not the end of the song.
abstract.cn: 失业是两个工作节拍之间的休止，而非乐曲的终结。

examples.en: The closure left nearly two hundred workers unemployed.
examples.cn: 工厂关闭使近两百名工人失业。

examples.en: Long-term unemployed people often need more than training to return to work.
examples.cn: 长期失业者重返职场往往需要的不仅是培训。

examples.en: The report measured unemployment among graduates for the first time.
examples.cn: 该报告首次统计了毕业生的失业情况。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安·因普洛伊德」——安（un 不）因普洛伊（employ 雇用）不成，德（ed）没人雇：失业

root: employ 经由古法语 employer「使用；聘用」溯至拉丁语 implicare「包住；缠住」（其分词形式衍生出「被占用」之义）；否定前缀 un- 来自古英语，与拉丁语 in- 同源，加于分词前构成否定；unemployed 即「未被雇用的」，词义随 employ 从「使用」收窄到「雇用」。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses of unemployed fan out from one empty space: hands without a job, machines without a task, money without a purpose, hours without an occupation.
sensesIntro.cn: unemployed 的八个义项从同一片空白展开：没有工作的手、没有任务的机器、没有用途的资金、没有事做的钟点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty badge hook where a working hand used to hang its card
core.cn: 核心意象：原本挂着工牌的挂钩如今空着

branches.en: THE PERSON: jobless, between jobs, and registered as seeking.
branches.cn: 个人线：没有工作、待业在两职之间、登记求职。

branches.en: THE THINGS: machines, money and hours left idle.
branches.cn: 器物线：闲置的机器、资金与时间。

branches.en: THE TALENT: skills with no outlet to work through.
branches.cn: 才能线：无处施展的技能。

branches.en: THE GROUP: a class of people defined by absence of work.
branches.cn: 群体线：被「无工作」定义的一类人。

branches.en: THE TIDE: seasonal and cyclical lows in employment.
branches.cn: 潮汐线：季节性与周期性的雇用低谷。

intro.en: Unemployed shows a Germanic prefix clipped onto a French verb, a very common English pattern.
intro.cn: unemployed 展示了日耳曼前缀接在法语动词上的组合，这是英语中极常见的模式。

latinIntro.en: The deep root is Latin implicare; cognates show the fold-and-use shift.
latinIntro.cn: 深层词根是拉丁语 implicare；同族词展示了「缠绕→使用」的语义转移。

items.example: It forms implicate with the Latin root.
items.exampleCN: 它与拉丁词根构成 implicate。

latinEntries.example: The ancestor of employ and imply.
latinEntries.exampleCN: employ 与 imply 的祖先。

latinEntries.example: It forms apply via Old French aplier.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 经由古法语 aplier 构成 apply。

derivatives.zh: 由本词变 -ed 为 -ment 构成，义为「失业；失业率；失业状态」
去掉否定前缀后的词基，义为「雇用；使用」
由词基加施动者后缀构成，义为「雇主」
由词基加后缀构成，义为「雇员」

definition_zh: 提交；屈从；主张
definition_en: to give something for others to consider, or to accept someone's power
core_image: 把文件双手递上去，也把头低下去
scene: 请在周五前提交申请。 Please submit your application by Friday.
sceneCN: 这里 submit 是「提交」（第 1 个义项）；句意：请在周五前提交申请。

derivatives.zh: 提交；屈服
顺从的
顺从地

senses.title: Hand in
senses.definition: to give a document or plan to someone in authority
senses.definitionCN: 把文件或计划交给有权处理的人
senses.example: Please submit your application by Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 请在周五前提交申请。
senses.why: This is the common official sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是常见的公务义项。

senses.title: Yield
senses.definition: to accept the power or control of another
senses.definitionCN: 接受他人的权力或控制
senses.example: They refused to submit to the new rules.
senses.exampleCN: 他们拒绝服从新规定。
senses.why: Handing something up becomes bowing down.
senses.whyCN: 把东西递上去，引申为低头服从。

senses.title: Argue
senses.definition: to suggest or argue formally
senses.definitionCN: 正式地提出或主张
senses.example: The lawyer submitted that the evidence was weak.
senses.exampleCN: 律师主张证据不足。
senses.why: Law places a claim before the court.
senses.whyCN: 法律把主张呈到法庭面前。

intro.en: Submit joins Latin sub, under, with mittere, to send.
intro.cn: submit 由拉丁语 sub（在下）与 mittere（送）组合而成。

items.en: Submittere meant to send under or yield.
items.cn: submittere 意为送到下面或屈服。

items.en: The past form submissus meant lowered.
items.cn: 过去分词 submissus 意为被放低的。

items.en: Submit meant to yield to power.
items.cn: submit 意为向权力屈服。

items.en: Submit meant to present a document.
items.cn: submit 意为呈交文件。

items.en: Submit gained the legal sense of arguing.
items.cn: submit 获得法律上主张的含义。

note.en: Submit is compared with look-alike words and with words for handing in.
note.cn: 把 submit 与形近词以及表示呈交的词作比较。

entries.definition: the top of a mountain
entries.definitionCN: 山顶

entries.definition: to agree that something is true
entries.definitionCN: 承认

entries.definition: to do something wrong or to promise
entries.definitionCN: 犯（错）；承诺

entries.definition: to give something formally
entries.definitionCN: 呈交

entries.definition: to give in to pressure
entries.definitionCN: 屈服

entries.definition: to suggest a plan
entries.definitionCN: 提议

normalIntro.en: Submit is to send something up to power, or to lower yourself before it.
normalIntro.cn: submit 是把东西呈给权力，或在权力面前低下头。

normal.en: Please submit your application by Friday.
normal.cn: 请在周五前提交申请。

normal.en: They refused to submit to the new rules.
normal.cn: 他们拒绝服从新规定。

normal.en: The lawyer submitted that the evidence was weak.
normal.cn: 律师主张证据不足。

normal.en: Submit the report before noon.
normal.cn: 中午之前提交报告。

normal.en: He submitted himself to the court.
normal.cn: 他服从法庭的裁决。

abstract.en: To submit a form is easy; to submit a will is not.
abstract.cn: 交一张表格很容易，交出一份意志却很难。

abstract.en: Every paper submitted carries a small piece of its writer.
abstract.cn: 每一份交上去的稿子，都带着作者的一小部分。

abstract.en: Some things should never be submitted to.
abstract.cn: 有些事，永远不该低头。

examples.en: Please submit your application by Friday.
examples.cn: 请在周五前提交申请。

examples.en: They refused to submit to the new rules.
examples.cn: 他们拒绝服从新规定。

examples.en: The lawyer submitted that the evidence was weak.
examples.cn: 律师主张证据不足。

dict_mnemonic.text: submit 是「提交」，也可表示「服从」或正式地「主张」；submit to 是服从于，submit an application 是提交申请，submit for approval 是提交审批。

root: 来自拉丁语 submittere（送到下面），由 sub（在下）与 mittere（送）组合；把东西送到上级面前是提交，把自己放到别人之下是屈服，把主张送到法庭面前则是正式提出。

sensesIntro.en: Submit means to hand in, to yield to power, or to argue formally.
sensesIntro.cn: submit 表示提交、向权力屈服，或正式提出主张。

core.en: Sending something upward, or lowering yourself.
core.cn: 把东西送上去，或把自己放低。

branches.en: Please submit your application by Friday.
branches.cn: 请在周五前提交申请。

branches.en: They refused to submit to the new rules.
branches.cn: 他们拒绝服从新规定。

branches.en: The lawyer submitted that the evidence was weak.
branches.cn: 律师主张证据不足。

branches.en: Handing in a document and bowing to power share an image.
branches.cn: 呈交文件和向权力低头，共享同一个意象。

branches.en: A claim is also handed to the court.
branches.cn: 主张也是递到法庭面前的一份东西。

intro.en: Submit doubles its final consonant and takes -sion and -ive.
intro.cn: submit 双写末尾辅音，并可加 -sion 和 -ive。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base miss- meant sent.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 miss- 意为送出。

items.example: She submits a report each week.
The deadline for submission is Friday.

latinEntries.example: Mittere gave English submit and admit.
latinEntries.exampleCN: mittere 演变为英语的 submit 和 admit。

definition_zh: 扩大；扩展；详述
definition_en: to become larger in size or amount; to grow in range or business; to give more detail
core_image: 一样东西向四周铺展开、占据更大空间
scene: 加热后金属会明显膨胀，占满缝隙。 When heated, the metal will expand and fill the gap.
sceneCN: 这里 expand 是「变大、膨胀」（第 1 个义项）；句意：加热后金属会明显膨胀，占满缝隙。

derivatives.zh: 扩张；膨胀
辽阔的；扩张的
可扩展的
广阔地；扩张地

senses.title: Grow larger
senses.definition: to become larger in size or amount
senses.definitionCN: 在体积或数量上变大
senses.example: Air expands as it warms.
senses.exampleCN: 空气受热会膨胀。
senses.why: The core image is spreading outward.
senses.whyCN: 核心形象是向四周铺展开。

senses.title: Widen range
senses.definition: to grow in range, size, or business
senses.definitionCN: 在范围、规模或业务上扩大
senses.example: The chain expanded to fifty stores.
senses.exampleCN: 这家连锁店扩展到了五十家门店。
senses.why: Physical growth is applied to organizations.
senses.whyCN: 物理上的变大被用于组织扩张。

senses.title: Add detail
senses.definition: to give more detail about something
senses.definitionCN: 对某事给出更多细节
senses.example: She expanded on her earlier comment.
senses.exampleCN: 她进一步说明了先前的评论。
senses.why: Spreading outward becomes spreading out an idea.
senses.whyCN: 向外铺开转化为把观点展开。

intro.en: Expand comes from Latin expandere, to spread out.
intro.cn: expand 源自拉丁语 expandere，意为「铺开」。

items.en: Expandere joins ex- (out) with pandere (to spread).
items.cn: expandere 由 ex-（向外）与 pandere（展开）构成。

items.en: Pandere describes spreading something open.
items.cn: pandere 表示把东西铺展开。

items.en: Expansus is the past participle of expandere.
items.cn: expansus 是 expandere 的过去分词。

items.en: Expanden first means to spread out.
items.cn: expanden 最初意为铺展开。

items.en: Expand grows to mean increase in size.
items.cn: expand 逐渐表示体积增大。

items.en: Expand on adds the sense of explaining more.
items.cn: expand on 增加了「进一步解释」之意。

note.en: Expand means to grow larger; expend means to use up.
note.cn: expand 是扩大，expend 则是花费、耗尽。

entries.definition: to use up money or energy
entries.definitionCN: 花费；耗尽

entries.definition: to explain in detail
entries.definitionCN: 详细解释

entries.definition: to think something will happen
entries.definitionCN: 预期；期待

entries.definition: to make or become bigger
entries.definitionCN: 扩大；放大

entries.definition: to make longer or wider
entries.definitionCN: 延长；扩展

entries.definition: to become larger and rounder
entries.definitionCN: 膨胀；肿起

normalIntro.en: Expand is about spreading out and getting bigger.
normalIntro.cn: expand 讲的是铺展开来、变得更大。

normal.en: The balloon expands as you blow into it.
normal.cn: 你一吹气，气球就膨胀起来。

normal.en: The company expanded into three new markets.
normal.cn: 这家公司扩展到了三个新市场。

normal.en: The teacher asked him to expand on his answer.
normal.cn: 老师让他进一步展开回答。

normal.en: Warm air expands and rises.
normal.cn: 暖空气膨胀上升。

normal.en: The library plans to expand its reading room.
normal.cn: 图书馆计划扩建阅览室。

abstract.en: Picture a small circle growing wider.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小圆圈越来越宽。

abstract.en: Imagine a map unfolding across a table.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图在桌上铺展开。

abstract.en: Think of a sponge swelling in water.
abstract.cn: 想象一块海绵在水里胀大。

examples.en: The metal expands when the temperature rises.
examples.cn: 温度升高时金属会膨胀。

examples.en: They hope to expand the program next year.
examples.cn: 他们希望明年扩大这个项目。

examples.en: The bridge design was expanded during the war.
examples.cn: 这座桥的设计在战争期间被扩充了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「expand」里有 ex（向外）+ pand（展开）：向外展开，就是「扩大」。

root: 拉丁语 expandere 由 ex-（向外）与 pandere（展开）构成，核心义「向外铺开」。

sensesIntro.en: Expand means to grow larger, widen a range, or explain in more detail.
sensesIntro.cn: expand 意为变大、扩大范围，或更详细地说明。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something spreading outward.
core.cn: 核心意象：某物向四周铺展开。

branches.en: Physical spreading is the core sense.
branches.cn: 物理上的铺开是核心义。

branches.en: Growth applies to companies and areas.
branches.cn: 「变大」被用于公司和地区。

branches.en: An idea is spread out with more words.
branches.cn: 观点用更多文字展开。

branches.en: Both involve increase in size or scope.
branches.cn: 两者都涉及体积或范围的增长。

branches.en: Widening scope and adding detail both extend.
branches.cn: 扩大范围与补充细节都是一种延伸。

intro.en: Expand carries the Latin prefix ex- and the verb pandere.
intro.cn: expand 含有拉丁前缀 ex- 与动词 pandere。

latinIntro.en: Latin expandere joins ex- (out) and pandere (to spread).
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 expandere 由 ex-（向外）与 pandere（展开）组合。

items.example: Pandere gives the idea of spreading.
Expandere is the direct source of expand.
items.exampleCN: expandere 是 expand 的直接来源。

items.example: Expand keeps the sense of spreading.
Expansion names the process of growing.

latinEntries.exampleCN: pandere 是表示展开的动词。

definition_zh: 管子；导管；烟斗；管乐器；管输送（动词）
definition_en: a tube that carries water or gas, a tube used for smoking, or to send something through such a tube
core_image: 一根空心长管：水从这头进去，从那头出来
scene: 工人蹲在路边的沟里，把一根根长管接到自来水干线上。 The workers laid a new pipe under the road to carry water to the village.
sceneCN: 这里是「管子」（第 1 个义项：输送水、气的空心管）；句意为工人们在路下铺设新水管把水引到村里。画面就是那根空心长管。

pos.zh: 用管道输送；以管乐器吹奏

derivatives.zh: pipe 加 line 合成，义为「管道；输油管」
pipe 加 -er 构成的施动名词，义为「吹笛人；管工」
pipe 的动名词，义为「管路；（衣服上的）滚边」
pipe 的过去分词作形容词，义为「用管道输送的」

senses.title: A tube carrying liquid or gas
senses.definition: a tube through which water, gas or oil flows
senses.definitionCN: 水、气或油流过的管子
senses.example: A burst pipe flooded the kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 一根爆裂的水管把厨房淹了。
senses.why: Latin pipare described a bird's peep, and the narrow tube took its name from the same thin, hollow sound-image.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 pipare 描摹鸟叫，细窄的管子因同样的细长中空的声音形象得名。

senses.title: A tube for smoking
senses.definition: a small tube with a bowl, used for smoking tobacco
senses.definitionCN: 带斗的短管，用来吸烟丝
senses.example: Grandfather lit his pipe by the fire.
senses.exampleCN: 祖父在炉边点燃烟斗。
senses.why: The tube shape of the instrument transferred to the smoking device, which is literally a small pipe held in the mouth.
senses.whyCN: 管形转指吸烟器具——那其实就是一支叼在嘴上的小管。

senses.title: A tube-shaped musical instrument
senses.definition: a tube that makes music when air is blown through it
senses.definitionCN: 吹气发声的管形乐器
senses.example: The shepherd played a pipe on the hillside.
senses.exampleCN: 牧羊人在山坡上吹笛。
senses.why: Blowing air through a hollow tube makes a whistling note, which is exactly what the bird-call word described.
senses.whyCN: 向空心管吹气发出哨音，正是鸟叫声那个词所描摹的声音。

senses.title: To carry through a tube
senses.definition: to send water, gas or oil through pipes
senses.definitionCN: 用管道把水、气或油送出去
senses.example: Gas is piped into every apartment in the block.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋楼的每套公寓都通了管道煤气。
senses.why: The noun became a verb by conversion: the tube itself does the sending.
senses.whyCN: 名词转类成动词：让管子自己去完成输送。

senses.title: To play a tune on pipes
senses.definition: to play music on a pipe or bagpipes
senses.definitionCN: 用管乐器或风笛奏乐
senses.example: A piper piped the guests into the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 吹笛人把宾客引进大厅。
senses.why: The instrument name turned into the verb for playing it.
senses.whyCN: 乐器名转成演奏它的动词。

senses.title: To speak in a high voice
senses.definition: to say something in a high, thin voice
senses.definitionCN: 用高而细的声音说话
senses.example: The child piped up with the answer.
senses.exampleCN: 那孩子尖着嗓子答了上来。
senses.why: The thin whistle of the tube matches the thin voice of a child, so the sound image moved to speech.
senses.whyCN: 细管的哨音对上孩子尖细的嗓音，声音形象便移到说话上。

senses.title: A cask of wine
senses.definition: a large cask, especially for wine, of about a hundred and twenty gallons
senses.definitionCN: 大酒桶，尤指约一百二十加仑的酒桶
senses.example: The cellar held a pipe of Portuguese wine.
senses.exampleCN: 酒窖里放着一大桶葡萄牙酒。
senses.why: Trade English borrowed the word for a big cask whose shape echoed the tube, though the sizes never matched.
senses.whyCN: 贸易英语借这个词指大桶，形状令人想起管子，尽管容量对不上。

intro.en: Pipe goes back to a Latin word for the chirping of birds, which passed through Old English and Old French to name every narrow hollow tube.
intro.cn: pipe 可追溯到一个拉丁词，本指鸟的啁啾，经古英语与古法语一路命名了所有细长的空心管。

items.en: Pipare meant to chirp or peep, an imitation of a bird's call.
items.cn: 拉丁语 pipare 意为啁啾、唧唧叫，是对鸟鸣的摹声。

items.en: Pipe appeared in Old English for a musical tube and for the sound it made.
items.cn: 古英语已有 pipe，指管乐器及其发出的声音。

items.en: Old French pipe carried the same senses and reinforced the English word.
items.cn: 古法语 pipe 带着同样的义项，强化了英语里的这个词。

items.en: The tube image spread to smoking devices, water conduits and, oddly, large wine casks.
items.cn: 管形意象扩散到吸烟具、输水管，还奇怪地指起大酒桶。

items.en: Conversion produced verbs for conveying through tubes, playing pipes and speaking in thin high voices.
items.cn: 转类造出管道输送、吹奏和尖声说话的动词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the pipe family and sound-alikes; the near-meaning group gathers tubes and conduits.
note.cn: 形近组收 pipe 词族与音近词；近义组收管类物。

entries.definition: One who plays pipes, as in the Pied Piper story.
entries.definitionCN: 吹笛者，如「花衣吹笛人」故事里那样。

entries.definition: A long line of pipes carrying oil or gas over distance.
entries.definitionCN: 远距离输送油气的一长串管道。

entries.definition: An evergreen tree; spelled one letter differently from pipe.
entries.definitionCN: 松树；与 pipe 仅差一个字母，词源无关。

entries.definition: A general hollow cylinder, usually smaller and often for testing or display.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指空心圆管，通常更细，常用于实验或显示。

entries.definition: A flexible tube, especially for spraying water.
entries.definitionCN: 软管，尤指喷水用的。

entries.definition: A channel or pipe that carries water or cables.
entries.definitionCN: 输送水或电缆的管道。

normalIntro.en: One image covers most senses: a hollow tube, and the whistling sound of blowing through it.
normalIntro.cn: 一个意象覆盖多数义项：一根空心管，以及吹过它时的哨音。

normal.en: The bird peeped, the tube whistled, the word pipare imitated both.
normal.cn: 鸟儿唧唧叫，管子呜呜响，pipare 一词摹拟了两者。

normal.en: A pipe has two lives: full of water underground, full of smoke upstairs.
normal.cn: pipe 有两种人生：地下的装满水，楼上的装满烟。

normal.en: Pipe down tells a noisy person to squeeze his voice into a thin pipe again.
normal.cn: pipe down 让吵闹的人把嗓音重新挤成细细的管声。

normal.en: The Pied Piper led rats away with the third sense, the musical tube.
normal.cn: 花衣吹笛人用第三个义项——会唱歌的管子——把老鼠引走了。

normal.en: Gas piped into homes shows the verb doing the tube's work.
normal.cn: 煤气 piped 进家，动词替管子干活。

abstract.en: A long silver tube running under the street, carrying something invisible.
abstract.cn: 一根银色长管在街道下延伸，运送着看不见的东西。

abstract.en: A curl of smoke rising from a curved tube in a fireside hand.
abstract.cn: 炉边一只手里弯管的烟斗升起一缕烟。

abstract.en: A thin high voice rising like a whistle over the classroom noise.
abstract.cn: 一声尖细的嗓音像哨音一样盖过教室的吵闹。

examples.en: The plumber replaced the rusty pipe in minutes.
examples.cn: 水管工几分钟就换掉了生锈的管子。

examples.en: He packed tobacco into his pipe and lit it.
examples.cn: 他把烟丝装进烟斗点着。

examples.en: Water is piped from the reservoir to every farm.
examples.cn: 水经管道从水库送往每个农场。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「排扑」——管道排走水、扑灭烟斗火；pipe 就是管子。

root: pipe 源自拉丁语 pipare（鸟啁啾，摹声词），经古英语与古法语进入英语；由「吹管的哨音」引申出管乐器、烟斗、输水管等义。

sensesIntro.en: From a bird's peep to every hollow tube: water pipes, tobacco pipes, organ pipes, and the verbs of sending, playing and squeaking.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一声鸟啼到所有空心管：水管、烟斗、管风琴，以及输送、吹奏和尖声说话的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow hollow tube that carries air, smoke, water or song.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根细窄的空心管，送气、送烟、送水、送歌。

branches.en: the conduit under the street
branches.cn: 街道下的导管

branches.en: the curved tube by the fire
branches.cn: 炉边的弯管

branches.en: the shepherd's whistle on the hill
branches.cn: 山坡上牧人的哨音

branches.en: the child's thin voice piping up
branches.cn: 孩子尖声抢答

branches.en: the tube and the sending through it
branches.cn: 管子与管中的输送

intro.en: Pipe is a short borrowed word that built its family almost entirely with English compounds and conversion.
intro.cn: pipe 是个短小的借词，词族几乎全靠英语复合与转类构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin pipare, a bird-call imitation, is the classical seed; English endings did the rest of the building.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pipare 这个摹声词是古典种子；其余的搭建全靠英语词尾。

items.meaning: speak suddenly in a high voice

definition_zh: 慈善；慈善机构；施舍
definition_en: kindness shown to others, an organization that helps people in need, or money and goods given to them
core_image: 一只手把面包递到另一只伸出的手里
scene: 教堂门口摆着一只募捐箱。 The charity provides meals for homeless families.
sceneCN: 这里 charity 指「慈善机构」（第 2 个义项：从事救济的组织）；句意是这家慈善机构为无家可归的家庭提供餐食。

derivatives.zh: 慈善的；宽厚的
仁慈地；以善意地

senses.title: Kindness toward others
senses.definition: kindness and understanding shown to other people
senses.definitionCN: 对他人的善意与体谅
senses.example: She treats everyone with charity.
senses.exampleCN: 她对每个人都心怀善意。
senses.why: Latin caritas meant dearness and Christian love, the warm root of the word.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 caritas 意为珍爱与基督之爱，是这个词温暖的根。

senses.title: An organization that helps
senses.definition: an organization set up to help people in need
senses.definitionCN: 为帮助困难者而设立的组织
senses.example: The charity provides meals for homeless families.
senses.exampleCN: 这家慈善机构为无家可归的家庭提供餐食。
senses.why: A body of people organized for love of neighbours took the name of the love itself.
senses.whyCN: 一群为关爱邻人而组织起来的人，借用了这份关爱本身的名字。

senses.title: Money or aid given
senses.definition: money or goods given to people who need them
senses.definitionCN: 给予困难者的钱款或物品
senses.example: He gave his spare coat to charity.
senses.exampleCN: 他把多余的外套捐给了慈善机构。
senses.why: The abstract love became concrete in the coins and clothes actually handed over.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的仁爱在真正交出的钱币与衣物中变得具体。

intro.en: Charity descends from a Latin word for dearness, which early Christian writers used for love of one's neighbours.
intro.cn: charity 源自拉丁语表示珍爱的词，早期基督教作家用它指对邻人的爱。

items.en: Carus meant dear or precious.
items.cn: 拉丁语 carus 意为珍贵的、亲爱的。

items.en: Caritas meant dearness and, in Christian use, loving kindness.
items.cn: caritas 意为珍爱，在基督教用法中指仁爱。

items.en: Charité carried both love and almsgiving.
items.cn: charité 同时带有爱与施舍之意。

items.en: English charity named Christian love and mercy.
items.cn: 英语 charity 指基督之爱与怜悯。

items.en: The word now also names the groups and gifts that express this love.
items.cn: 如今该词也指表达这份爱的组织与捐赠。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the charitable stem, while the meaning group lists kindness and aid words.
note.cn: 形近组共享 charitable 词干，近义组列出善意与援助类词。

entries.definition: generous in giving help
entries.definitionCN: 乐于助人的

entries.definition: in a kind and generous way
entries.definitionCN: 以仁慈宽厚的方式

entries.definition: more than one charity
entries.definitionCN: 慈善机构的复数形式

entries.definition: the quality of being friendly and caring
entries.definitionCN: 友善关怀的品质

entries.definition: help given to those in need
entries.definitionCN: 给予困难者的帮助

entries.definition: money given to a good cause
entries.definitionCN: 捐给公益事业的钱

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the dear root, the charity shop phrase and the gift sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用「珍爱」词根、短语 charity shop 以及捐赠义。

normal.en: Charity and cherish both come from a Latin word for something dear.
normal.cn: charity 与 cherish 都来自拉丁语中表示珍贵之物的词。

normal.en: A charity shop turns donated things into money for the poor.
normal.cn: charity shop 把捐赠物变成给穷人的钱。

normal.en: Out of charity means the act comes from kindness, not duty.
normal.cn: out of charity 意为出于善心而非义务。

normal.en: Charity begins at home is the proverb that keeps the word warm.
normal.cn: Charity begins at home 这句谚语让这个词保持温度。

normal.en: The plural charities covers several organizations at once.
normal.cn: 复数 charities 一次指好几家机构。

abstract.en: Picture a hand passing bread through a narrow doorway.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手从窄门口递出面包。

abstract.en: Picture a collection box heavy with small coins.
abstract.cn: 想象一只装满零钱的募捐箱。

abstract.en: Picture a shop window full of second-hand coats.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇摆满旧外套的商店橱窗。

examples.en: The concert raised money for local charities.
examples.cn: 音乐会为当地慈善机构筹款。

examples.en: He never speaks of anyone without charity.
examples.cn: 他谈起任何人都带着善意。

examples.en: The old books were sold for charity.
examples.cn: 那些旧书被卖掉用于慈善。

dict_mnemonic.text: charity 与 cherish 同源：心里珍爱一个人，才会伸手施舍，这就是慈善。

root: 源自拉丁语 carus（珍贵的）及其派生 caritas（珍爱、仁爱），经古法语 charité 进入英语；与 cherish 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Dearness becomes Christian love, love becomes an organized body, and the body turns into gifts of money and goods.
sensesIntro.cn: 珍爱变成基督之爱，爱变成有组织的团体，团体再化为钱物捐赠。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: love that reaches out to a neighbour.
core.cn: 核心意象：伸向邻人的那份爱。

branches.en: Treating people with charity is the oldest sense.
branches.cn: 以善意待人是最古老的义项。

branches.en: A charity is a body organized around that love.
branches.cn: 慈善机构是围绕这份爱组织起来的团体。

branches.en: Giving to charity turns feeling into goods.
branches.cn: 捐给慈善把情感变成实物。

branches.en: Both senses keep the idea of giving freely.
branches.cn: 两个义项都保留自愿给予的意思。

branches.en: Organizations and gifts depend on each other.
branches.cn: 机构与捐赠彼此依存。

intro.en: Charity keeps the car- dear root in charitable and charitably.
intro.cn: charity 在 charitable 与 charitably 中保留 car-「珍爱」词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin carus and caritas are the dear thing and the love that produced charity.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 carus 与 caritas 是产出 charity 的「珍贵之物」与「爱」。

items.exampleCN: 两家慈善机构分享了这笔基金。

latinEntries.example: Carus is the root of charity.
latinEntries.exampleCN: carus 是 charity 的词根。

definition_zh: 辞职；辞呈；顺从
definition_en: the act of leaving a job, the letter announcing it, or patient acceptance
core_image: 一封印着公司抬头的信，最后一行是签名
scene: 她把辞呈折好放进信封，交给人事经理。 She folded her resignation and handed it to the personnel manager.
sceneCN: 这里 resignation 是「辞呈」（第 2 个义项：宣布辞职的信件）；句意：她把辞呈折好放进信封，交给人事经理。

derivatives.zh: 辞职；放弃
无奈的；顺从的
无奈地

senses.title: The act of leaving a job
senses.definition: the act of formally giving up a job or position
senses.definitionCN: 正式放弃工作或职位的行为
senses.example: His resignation surprised the whole department.
senses.exampleCN: 他的辞职让整个部门都很意外。
senses.why: The -ation noun names the completed act of resigning.
senses.whyCN: -ation 名词指已完成的辞职行为。

senses.title: The letter announcing it
senses.definition: a formal letter in which someone states that they are leaving their job
senses.definitionCN: 正式说明将要离职的信件
senses.example: She folded her resignation and handed it to the manager.
senses.exampleCN: 她把辞呈折好交给经理。
senses.why: The document that carries the decision takes the same name as the act.
senses.whyCN: 承载这一决定的文件与行为同名。

senses.title: Patient acceptance
senses.definition: the calm acceptance of something unpleasant that cannot be changed
senses.definitionCN: 对无法改变的坏事平静接受
senses.example: He accepted the delay with resignation.
senses.exampleCN: 他无奈地接受了延误。
senses.why: Giving up struggle in the mind is the inward form of resigning.
senses.whyCN: 在内心里放弃挣扎，是 resign 的向内形式。

intro.en: Resignation is the noun of resign, from Latin resignare, to unseal or cancel, plus the ending -ation.
intro.cn: resignation 是 resign 的名词，来自拉丁语 resignare（开封、注销），加词尾 -ation。

items.en: Signare means to mark or seal.
items.cn: signare 意为标记或盖章。

items.en: Resignare means to unseal or cancel.
items.cn: resignare 意为开封或注销。

items.en: Resigner means to resign or give up.
items.cn: resigner 意为辞职、放弃。

items.en: Middle English resignen gives the base verb.
items.cn: 中古英语 resignen 提供基础动词。

items.en: Resignation appears as the act of giving up office.
items.cn: 到 14 世纪，resignation 指放弃职位的行为。

items.en: The sense of patient acceptance becomes common.
items.cn: 到 17 世纪，表示「平静接受」的义项流行起来。

note.en: Resignation is the -ation noun of resign, and it sits near its family and near words for departure and acceptance.
note.cn: resignation 是 resign 的 -ation 名词，与自身词族以及表示离开和接受的词相邻。

entries.definition: to leave a job officially
entries.definitionCN: 辞职

entries.definition: accepting something unwillingly
entries.definitionCN: 无奈的；顺从的

entries.definition: in a patient way
entries.definitionCN: 无奈地

entries.definition: the act of leaving a place or job
entries.definitionCN: 离开；离职

entries.definition: advance warning that you are leaving a job
entries.definitionCN: 离职通知期

entries.definition: the act of agreeing to something
entries.definitionCN: 接受

normalIntro.en: Resignation is resign plus -ation: the act, the letter, or the calm acceptance that follows.
normalIntro.cn: resignation 是 resign 加 -ation：辞职行为、辞呈，或随之而来的平静接受。

normal.en: Submit one's resignation is the formal phrase.
normal.cn: submit one's resignation 是正式说法。

normal.en: A letter of resignation stays on file.
normal.cn: 辞职信会留在档案里。

normal.en: With resignation means accepting something sadly but calmly.
normal.cn: with resignation 意为悲伤却平静地接受。

normal.en: The same word names the act and the document.
normal.cn: 同一个词既指行为，也指文件。

normal.en: Compare notice: notice is the warning period, while resignation is the decision.
normal.cn: 对比 notice：notice 是通知期，resignation 是决定本身。

abstract.en: Picture an envelope sealed with a company stamp.
abstract.cn: 想象一个盖着公司印章的信封。

abstract.en: Imagine a desk cleared of personal things.
abstract.cn: 想象一张清空了私人物品的办公桌。

abstract.en: Think of a shoulder dropping in a long queue.
abstract.cn: 想象在长队里肩膀无奈地垮下来。

examples.en: His resignation surprised the whole department.
examples.cn: 他的辞职让整个部门都很意外。

examples.en: She folded her resignation and handed it to the manager.
examples.cn: 她把辞呈折好交给经理。

examples.en: He accepted the delay with resignation.
examples.cn: 他无奈地接受了延误。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「resign + ation」——辞职这件事、这封信，或不得不接受的平静；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 signare（标记）→ resignare（注销）→ 古法语 resigner → 中古英语 resignen → resign ＋ -ation → resignation。

sensesIntro.en: The noun names the decision to leave, the paper that carries it, and the quiet acceptance left when struggle ends.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个名词指离开的决定、承载决定的文件，以及挣扎结束后留下的平静接受。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a signed letter in an envelope on a cleared desk.
core.cn: 核心意象：清空的桌上放着装好签字的信封。

branches.en: The act of leaving is the legal core.
branches.cn: 离职行为，是法律层面的核心。

branches.en: The letter is the physical form of the decision.
branches.cn: 辞呈是决定的有形形式。

branches.en: Patient acceptance is the inward echo of leaving.
branches.cn: 平静接受是离职在内心的回声。

branches.en: The act and the letter usually appear together.
branches.cn: 行为与信件通常一起出现。

branches.en: A formal exit and a quiet surrender both involve letting go.
branches.cn: 正式退出与安静顺从都涉及「放手」。

intro.en: Resignation is an English -ation noun built on resign, from Latin resignare.
intro.cn: resignation 是建立在 resign 上的英语 -ation 名词，源于拉丁语 resignare。

latinIntro.en: Latin signare means to mark, and resignare means to unseal or cancel.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 signare 意为标记，resignare 意为开封或注销。

items.example: Re- adds the idea of giving back.
Resigner carries the verb into French.
items.exampleCN: resigner 把这个动词带入法语。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的词尾

definition_zh: 巨人；巨头；巨大的
definition_en: a huge person in stories, a very large and powerful company or person, or very large
core_image: 一个高大的身影从云层里俯身看着山下的村庄
scene: 故事里的巨人一步跨过了小河。 The giant in the story stepped over the stream.
sceneCN: 这里 giant 是「巨人」（第 1 个义项）；句意：故事里的巨人一步跨过了小河。

derivatives.zh: 巨大的；庞大的
女巨人

senses.title: Huge story figure
senses.definition: an imaginary person of very great size and strength
senses.definitionCN: 想象中体型和力量极大的存在
senses.example: The giant in the story stepped over the stream.
senses.exampleCN: 故事里的巨人一步跨过了小河。
senses.why: The word came from the giants of Greek myth.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自希腊神话中的巨人族。

senses.title: Huge power
senses.definition: a very large and powerful company or person in a field
senses.definitionCN: 某一领域中规模与影响力极大的公司或人物
senses.example: She works for a tech giant.
senses.exampleCN: 她在一家科技巨头工作。
senses.why: Great size became a metaphor for great power.
senses.whyCN: 巨大的体型成了巨大力量的比喻。

senses.title: Very large
senses.definition: much larger than usual
senses.definitionCN: 比通常大得多
senses.example: The project was a giant step forward.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目是向前迈出的巨大一步。
senses.why: The noun turned into an adjective of size.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词转化成了表示尺寸的形容词。

intro.en: Giant came to English through French from the Greek giants of myth.
intro.cn: giant 经法语进入英语，源头是希腊神话中的巨人。

items.en: Gigas named a member of a race of huge beings.
items.cn: gigas 指巨人族的一员。

items.en: Gigas was taken into Latin with the same meaning.
items.cn: gigas 以同样含义进入拉丁语。

items.en: The word appeared in French as geant.
items.cn: 这个词以 geant 的形式出现在法语中。

items.en: English borrowed it as giant.
items.cn: 英语借入时写作 giant。

items.en: It extended to huge companies and very large things.
items.cn: 它的含义扩展到庞大的公司和极大的事物。

note.en: Giant is compared with look-alike words and words for huge beings and things.
note.cn: 把 giant 与形近词以及表示巨大存在或事物的词作比较。

entries.definition: to allow or give formally
entries.definitionCN: 授予；准许

entries.definition: very thin and bony
entries.definitionCN: 瘦削的

entries.definition: a wish-granting spirit
entries.definitionCN: 精灵

entries.definition: a person or thing of enormous strength
entries.definitionCN: 巨人；巨擘

entries.definition: a hugely large statue or person
entries.definitionCN: 巨型雕像；巨人

entries.definition: a huge extinct elephant, or something very large
entries.definitionCN: 猛犸象；庞然大物

normalIntro.en: A giant is size that changes the scale of everything else.
normalIntro.cn: giant 就是会改变其他一切尺度的巨大。

normal.en: The giant in the story stepped over the stream.
normal.cn: 故事里的巨人一步跨过了小河。

normal.en: She works for a tech giant.
normal.cn: 她在一家科技巨头工作。

normal.en: The project was a giant step forward.
normal.cn: 这个项目是向前迈出的巨大一步。

normal.en: The gentle giant helped the children.
normal.cn: 那位温和的大块头帮助了孩子们。

normal.en: Landing on the moon was a giant leap.
normal.cn: 登上月球是一次巨大的飞跃。

abstract.en: Great size is only great until it meets something larger.
abstract.cn: 巨大的体型，直到遇见更大的东西之前才算巨大。

abstract.en: Power is a giant that sleeps lightly.
abstract.cn: 权力是一个睡得不安稳的巨人。

abstract.en: Small hands can still move giant stones with patience.
abstract.cn: 小手只要有耐心，也能挪动巨石。

examples.cn: 故事里的巨人一步跨过了小河。

dict_mnemonic.text: giant 来自希腊神话中的巨人族 gigas：体型巨大的人就是「巨人」，规模巨大的公司就是「巨头」，a giant step 是「巨大的一步」。

root: 来自希腊语 gigas（巨人族），经拉丁语和古法语 geant 进入英语，核心义「体型与力量极大的存在」。

sensesIntro.en: Giant means a huge figure in stories, a very powerful company or person, or something very large.
sensesIntro.cn: giant 意为故事中的巨人、极其强大的公司或人物，或巨大的事物。

core.en: Great size, whether of body or of power.
core.cn: 无论是身体还是力量的巨大。

branches.en: A huge shape bends down over a village.
branches.cn: 一个巨大的身影俯身看向村庄。

branches.en: One company sets the pace for an industry.
branches.cn: 一家公司决定了整个行业的节奏。

branches.en: One step covers the length of a field.
branches.cn: 一步就跨过一整块田地的长度。

branches.en: Storybook size and real size borrow the same word.
branches.cn: 故事里的巨大与现实中的巨大借用同一个词。

branches.en: Market power wears the face of an old giant.
branches.cn: 市场力量长着一张古老巨人的脸。

intro.en: Giant stands beside a family of words for enormous size.
intro.cn: giant 与一组表示极大尺寸的词并列。

latinIntro.en: Greek gigas, Latin gigas, both named a giant.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 gigas 与拉丁语 gigas 都指巨人。

items.example: The tale tells of two giants.
items.exampleCN: 这个故事讲的是两个巨人。

items.example: A gigantic wave hit the shore.

items.exampleCN: 这个计划失败得一塌糊涂。
他们买了一个特大号披萨。

items.example: The star became a red supergiant.
items.exampleCN: 这颗恒星变成了红超巨星。

items.example: His giantlike shadow crossed the wall.
items.exampleCN: 他巨人般的影子掠过墙面。

latinEntries.example: Gigas is the root of giant.
latinEntries.exampleCN: gigas 是 giant 的词根。
giganticus 孕育了英语的 gigantic。

definition_zh: 代码；密码；法典；编码
definition_en: a system of words or symbols used to represent information, a set of written rules or laws, or to write instructions for a computer
core_image: 把想法压缩成一串只有圈内人看得懂的符号
scene: 程序员盯着屏幕，把一段指令敲进编辑器。 She wrote the code that runs the whole system.
sceneCN: 这里 code 指「代码」（第 1 个义项：计算机指令）；句意是她写下了运行整个系统的代码。

derivatives.zh: 程序员；编码员
编码；编程
解码；破译
编码；把…译成密码
编纂成法典；整理成系统

senses.title: Instructions for a computer
senses.definition: a set of instructions written for a computer program
senses.definitionCN: 为计算机程序编写的一组指令
senses.example: The code crashed when the file was too large.
senses.exampleCN: 文件太大时，这段代码崩溃了。
senses.why: A machine cannot read our words, so we hand it a private alphabet.
senses.whyCN: 机器读不懂人的语言，于是我们交给它一套私密字母表。

senses.title: A secret system of signs
senses.definition: a system of letters or symbols used to keep a message secret
senses.definitionCN: 用来保密信息的字母或符号系统
senses.example: The spy refused to give up the code.
senses.exampleCN: 那名间谍拒绝交出密码。
senses.why: Codes once kept messages safe from anyone without the key.
senses.whyCN: 密码曾让没有钥匙的人无法读懂信息。

senses.title: A set of written rules
senses.definition: a written set of laws or rules that govern behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 规范行为的一整套成文法律或规则
senses.example: Every member must follow the club's code.
senses.exampleCN: 每位成员都必须遵守俱乐部的准则。
senses.why: Law is also a code: signs arranged so that people can read what is allowed.
senses.whyCN: 法律也是一种代码：符号排好，让人读出什么被允许。

intro.en: Code traces back to Latin codex, the wooden tablet used for writing.
intro.cn: code 上溯拉丁语 codex，即用来书写的木板书板。

items.en: Codex meant a block of wood and then a tablet for writing.
items.cn: codex 本指一块木头，后指书写用的板。

items.en: A codex of laws held rules in one ordered book.
items.cn: 一部法典把规则收在一本有序的书里。

items.en: French code carried the legal sense into English.
items.cn: 法语 code 把法律义带进了英语。

items.en: The word spread from law to any organised set of signs.
items.cn: 这个词从法律扩展到任何有组织的符号系统。

items.en: Computing made code the everyday word for program text.
items.cn: 计算机让 code 成为程序文本的日常说法。

note.en: The look-alike group holds short words that differ from code by one letter, while the meaning group covers secret writing and instruction sets.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 code 只差一两个字母的短词，近义组涉及密文与指令集。

entries.definition: a shape with a round base and a point
entries.definitionCN: 底面为圆、顶端带尖的形状

entries.definition: a long thin flexible rope
entries.definitionCN: 细长而有弹性的绳

entries.definition: to deal successfully with a hard situation
entries.definitionCN: 成功应付困难局面

entries.definition: a secret way of writing messages
entries.definitionCN: 书写密文的秘密方式

entries.definition: a set of instructions that makes a computer work
entries.definitionCN: 让计算机工作的一组指令

entries.definition: a rule made by a government for all people
entries.definitionCN: 政府为所有人制定的规则

normalIntro.en: These hooks connect the wooden tablet, the secret letter and the lines a programmer types.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把木板书板、密信和程序员敲下的行行字符连在一起。

normal.en: A codex was a wooden tablet, so code begins with something written down.
normal.cn: codex 是木板书板，所以 code 的起点是写下来的东西。

normal.en: Laws were gathered into codes long before computers existed.
normal.cn: 早在计算机出现之前，法律就被汇编成法典。

normal.en: A code keeps a message closed to outsiders, like a locked box.
normal.cn: 密码把信息对局外人锁住，像一只上锁的箱子。

normal.en: Add the prefix de and decode means opening that box again.
normal.cn: 加上前缀 de，decode 就是把那只箱子重新打开。

normal.en: Code and decode sit at opposite ends of one message.
normal.cn: code 与 decode 位于同一条信息的两端。

abstract.en: Picture a monk copying laws onto a thick wooden tablet.
abstract.cn: 想象一位修士把法律条文抄到厚厚的木板上。

abstract.en: Picture a page of symbols that only one reader can unlock.
abstract.cn: 想象一页符号，只有一位读者能把它解开。

abstract.en: Picture green lines of text scrolling down a dark screen.
abstract.cn: 想象一行行绿色字符在暗屏上向下滚动。

examples.en: He spent the night fixing a bug in the code.
examples.cn: 他花了一整夜修复代码里的一个错误。

examples.en: The letter was written in a code that nobody could read.
examples.cn: 这封信是用没人能读懂的密码写的。

examples.en: The new code on dress makes the office more relaxed.
examples.cn: 新的着装准则让办公室氛围更轻松。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 code 记成一本锁起来的符号册：翻开来是指令，锁起来是密码。

root: 源自拉丁语 codex（木板书板），经法语 code 进入英语，由成文法典扩展为符号系统与计算机指令。

sensesIntro.en: From a written tablet to a book of laws, then to hidden signs and machine instructions.
sensesIntro.cn: 从书写的木板，到成文法典，再到隐秘符号与机器指令。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a string of signs that carries meaning only to those who hold the key.
core.cn: 核心意象：一串只有持钥匙者才读得懂的符号。

branches.en: Machine code is the newest and most common sense today.
branches.cn: 机器代码是今天最新也最常用的义项。

branches.en: A cipher hides a message behind unfamiliar signs.
branches.cn: 密码用陌生的符号把信息藏起来。

branches.en: A code of law arranges rules in one readable order.
branches.cn: 法典把规则排成一个可读的顺序。

branches.en: Both senses rest on a fixed system of signs.
branches.cn: 两个义项都建立在固定的符号系统上。

branches.en: A programmer and a lawmaker both write codes that others must follow.
branches.cn: 程序员与立法者都在写别人必须遵循的代码。

intro.en: Code takes Latin prefixes easily, so its family is built on en-, de- and -ify.
intro.cn: code 很容易接拉丁前缀，家族靠 en-、de- 与 -ify 构建。

latinIntro.en: The base codex is Latin for a writing tablet, and codex still names an ancient book.
latinIntro.cn: 词基 codex 在拉丁语中指书写板，今天 codex 仍指古籍抄本。

items.meaning: more than one code, or he writes instructions
items.example: The two codes must match exactly.
items.exampleCN: 两套代码必须完全一致。

items.meaning: put into a code or written as a program
items.example: The message was coded before it was sent.
items.exampleCN: 这条信息在发送前已被加密。

items.meaning: the work of writing computer programs
items.example: Coding takes patience more than speed.
items.exampleCN: 编程更需要耐心而不是速度。

items.meaning: a person who writes computer code
items.example: She hired a coder for the new app.
items.exampleCN: 她为这款新应用请了一位程序员。

items.meaning: to change information into a code
items.exampleCN: 这台设备把每通电话都编码。

items.meaning: to turn a code back into plain meaning
items.meaningCN: 把代码还原为明白的意思
items.example: They needed a key to decode the file.
items.exampleCN: 他们需要一把钥匙来解码这个文件。

items.meaning: to arrange rules into a clear system
items.meaningCN: 把规则整理成清晰的体系
items.example: The team codified its safety rules.
items.exampleCN: 这个团队把安全规则编纂成文。

items.meaning: the act of arranging rules into a code
items.example: The codification of the law took years.
items.exampleCN: 这部法律的编纂花了数年。

items.meaning: a pattern of lines read by a machine
a group of letters and numbers used in an address
items.meaningCN: 地址中使用的邮政编码

latinEntries.meaning: a wooden tablet or a bound manuscript
latinEntries.example: The oldest codex in the library is under glass.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 馆中最古老的抄本放在玻璃罩下。

definition_zh: 无辜的；清白的；天真的；无害的
definition_en: not guilty of a crime or wrongdoing, or naive, pure, and free from harmful intent
core_image: 未染尘埃的白：没有做过错事的人
scene: 法庭里，被告紧握双手等待宣判，旁听席一片寂静。 The jury declared the defendant innocent after only one hour.
sceneCN: 这里 innocent 是「无罪的」（第 1 个义项：未犯被指控之罪）；句意：陪审团仅用一小时便裁定被告无罪。

collocations.zh: 未经判罪前先推定无辜

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「清白；天真」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「无辜地；天真地」
反义词，义为「有罪的；内疚的」

senses.title: Not guilty of a crime
senses.definition: not having committed the crime or wrongdoing charged
senses.definitionCN: 未犯下被指控的罪行
senses.example: The court found him innocent of all charges.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭裁定他所有罪名均不成立。
senses.why: The Latin root means not harming, and one who has not harmed is not guilty.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「不加害」，未加害者即清白。

senses.title: Naive and without experience of evil
senses.definition: simple, trusting, and unaware of wrongdoing or danger
senses.definitionCN: 单纯、轻信、不知世故与危险
senses.example: She had an innocent trust in strangers.
senses.exampleCN: 她对陌生人抱着天真的信任。
senses.why: One who has never done harm often does not expect harm from others.
senses.whyCN: 从未加害之人，往往也料不到他人会加害。

senses.title: Harmless, without intent to hurt
senses.definition: causing no harm, or not meant to offend or injure
senses.definitionCN: 不造成伤害，或无意冒犯
senses.example: It was an innocent question, not an attack.
senses.exampleCN: 那是个无心的问题，并非攻击。
senses.why: Back to the root: what does not harm is innocent.
senses.whyCN: 回到词根：不加害者即 innocent。

intro.en: Innocent says it in Latin: not-harming.
intro.cn: innocent 用拉丁语道明本义：不加害。

items.en: Latin innocens meant not injuring, from in- (not) plus nocere (to harm).
items.cn: 拉丁语 innocens 意为「不加害」，由 in-（不）加 nocere（伤害）构成。

items.en: Church writers used the word for moral purity and sinlessness.
items.cn: 教会作家用该词指道德纯洁、无罪污。

items.en: Old French borrowed it as innocent with both legal and moral shades.
items.cn: 古法语借入 innocent，兼具法律与道德两重色彩。

items.en: English took the word in the thirteenth century, early on often about simple folk.
items.cn: 英语十三世纪引入，早期多形容质朴之人。

items.en: Law fixed the not-guilty sense; everyday speech favors the naive and harmless senses.
items.cn: 法律固定了「无罪」义；日常口语偏爱「天真」与「无害」义。

note.en: The nocere root family warns of harm; near-words share purity or guiltlessness.
note.cn: nocere 词根家族皆与「害」有关；近义词共享纯真或无咎之意。

entries.definition: the state of being innocent

entries.definition: harmless, not likely to offend

entries.definition: harmful; rare literary word
entries.definitionCN: 有害的；生僻书面词

entries.definitionCN: 天真的；缺乏阅历的

entries.definition: free from blame

normal.en: Law phrase: innocent until proven guilty.

normal.en: Noun pair: innocence is the state.

normal.en: Opposite: guilty, the verdict of the harmed.
normal.cn: 反义：guilty，加害之判。

abstract.en: A white dove resting on a courthouse window.
abstract.cn: 法庭窗台上歇着一只白鸽。

abstract.en: A child's open palm with nothing to hide.
abstract.cn: 孩子摊开的掌心，一无遮掩。

abstract.en: Snow on a city street, unmarked by any footprint.
abstract.cn: 雪落城市街头，未留一枚脚印。

examples.en: The innocent bystander was caught in the middle of the quarrel.
examples.cn: 无辜的旁观者被卷入了争吵的中心。

examples.en: Her innocent smile hid a sharp mind.
examples.cn: 她天真的笑容下藏着机敏的头脑。

examples.en: The pesticide was considered innocent until tests proved otherwise.
examples.cn: 这种杀虫剂在检测证明有问题之前被视为无害。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「你心善」——你心地善良，从没想过伤害别人。

root: 拉丁语 innocens（不加害的），由 in-（不）加 nocere（伤害）构成；经古法语 innocent 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Not-harming becomes not-guilty, then naive, then harmless.
sensesIntro.cn: 「不加害」依次引申为「无罪」「天真」「无害」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the hand that has harmed nothing
core.cn: 核心意象：从未伤害过任何东西的手

branches.en: the courtroom verdict of no guilt
branches.cn: 法庭上的无罪判定

branches.en: the purity of the untested heart
branches.cn: 未经世事之心的纯净

branches.en: words and acts free of malice
branches.cn: 不带恶意的言行

branches.en: guiltlessness and purity reinforce each other
branches.cn: 无咎与纯真相互印证

branches.en: the naive also strike no blows
branches.cn: 天真者亦不伤人

intro.en: A negative prefix meets a harm root.
intro.cn: 否定前缀遇上「伤害」词根。

latinIntro.en: Nocere (to harm) left its mark across English.
latinIntro.cn: nocere（伤害）在英语中留下多处印记。

senses.title: The bringing of goods
senses.definition: the act of taking goods, letters or food to a customer
senses.definitionCN: 把货物、信件或食物送到顾客手中的行为
senses.example: The shop offers free delivery within the city.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店在本城范围内免运费送货。
senses.why: The last metre of a journey is the one the buyer pays for.
senses.whyCN: 一段路的最后一米，才是买家真正花钱买的那段。

senses.title: The way words are spoken
senses.definition: the manner in which a speech or song is given to listeners
senses.definitionCN: 把讲话或歌曲呈现给听众的方式
senses.example: Her delivery was calm and clear.
senses.exampleCN: 她的表达从容而清楚。
senses.why: The same sentence can be handed over gently or dropped.
senses.whyCN: 同一句话，可以轻轻递过去，也可以扔过去。

senses.title: The birth of a child
senses.definition: the act of a baby coming out of its mother's body
senses.definitionCN: 婴儿从母亲身体里出来的过程
senses.example: The delivery went well and both were healthy.
senses.exampleCN: 分娩顺利，母子都健康。
senses.why: A new life also has to be carried out into the air.
senses.whyCN: 新的生命，也要被送到空气里来。

intro.en: Delivery is deliver plus -y, and deliver goes back to Latin liberare, to set free.
intro.cn: delivery 是 deliver 加 -y，而 deliver 上溯到拉丁语 liberare（使自由）。

items.en: Liberare meant to release a person from a hold.
items.cn: liberare 意为把一个人从束缚中放开。

items.en: Delivrer meant to hand over or to set free.
items.cn: delivrer 意为交出，也意为释放。

items.en: The noun delivery named both rescue and handing over.
items.cn: 名词 delivery 同时指解救与交出。

items.en: Trade gave it the everyday sense of goods arriving.
items.cn: 商业给了它「货物送达」这个日常意思。

items.en: It now also covers the manner of speaking and the birth of a child.
items.cn: 如今它也指说话的方式与婴儿的出生。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the liver shape, and the meaning group names what arrives at a door.
note.cn: 形近组共用 liver 这个形状，近义组则指送到门口的那批东西。

entries.definition: to bring goods to a place
entries.definitionCN: 把货物送到某处

entries.definition: the uniform worn by servants

entries.definition: the state of being set free
entries.definitionCN: 被解救的状态

entries.definition: a load of goods sent together
entries.definitionCN: 一起运出的一批货物

entries.definition: goods sent to someone to be sold
entries.definitionCN: 送去代销的一批货物

entries.definition: the act of passing something to another
entries.definitionCN: 把东西交给另一方的行为

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a name on a box and end with a sentence handed gently to a hall.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从箱子上贴着的名字开始，落到一句被轻轻递到大厅里的话。

normal.en: The box knows your name before you do.
normal.cn: 箱子先知道你的名字，你才知道它到了。

normal.en: Good delivery is quiet: no dropped corners, no broken eggs.
normal.cn: 好的送货很安静：不摔角，不碎蛋。

normal.en: The same line, delivered slowly, becomes a different line.
normal.cn: 同一句话，慢慢递出去，就成了另一句话。

normal.en: A promise and a parcel both end at a door.
normal.cn: 承诺与包裹，最后都停在一扇门前。

normal.en: Delivery is the noun that deliver leaves behind.
normal.cn: delivery 就是 deliver 留下的名词。

abstract.en: Picture a strip of tape being pressed down on a box.
abstract.cn: 想象一条胶带被按在纸箱上。

abstract.en: Picture a signature made quickly with a borrowed pen.
abstract.cn: 想象用借来的笔匆匆签下一个名字。

abstract.en: Picture a room going quiet so a voice can be heard.
abstract.cn: 想象一屋子人安静下来，好让一个声音被听见。

examples.en: The shop offers free delivery within the city.
examples.cn: 这家店在本城范围内免运费送货。

examples.en: Her delivery was calm and clear.
examples.cn: 她的表达从容而清楚。

examples.en: The delivery went well and both were healthy.
examples.cn: 分娩顺利，母子都健康。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 delivery 记成「递礼物」：把礼物递到门口，就是投递；递话递得好，就是表达。

root: 由 deliver 加名词词尾 -y 构成。deliver 出自拉丁语 liberare（使自由）与古法语 delivrer，先指解救与交出，后来「把货物送到」成为日常意思，又引申出说话的表达方式与婴儿的分娩。

sensesIntro.en: From a box at the door, to a voice in a hall, to a new life carried into the air.
sensesIntro.cn: 从门口的箱子，到大厅里的声音，再到被送到空气里的新生命。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a box set down, with a name written on it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个箱子放下，上面写着名字。

branches.en: The first sense ends with goods in the buyer's hands.
branches.cn: 第一个义项以货物到买家手中结束。

branches.en: The second sense hands words to listeners instead.
branches.cn: 第二个义项递出去的是话，给的是听众。

branches.en: The third sense is a body arriving into the world.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是一个身体来到世上。

branches.en: Goods and words are both judged by how they arrive.
branches.cn: 货物与话，都要看它们是怎么到的。

branches.en: Both senses need care at the moment of handing over.
branches.cn: 两个义项在交出的那一刻都需要小心。

intro.en: Delivery sits at the noun end of a family that includes deliver, deliverer and deliverable.
intro.cn: delivery 站在这一族的名词一端，同族还有 deliver、deliverer、deliverable。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is liberare, to free, with de- meaning away.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁词基是 liberare（使自由），前缀 de- 表示离开。

items.meaning: the act of bringing or handing over

items.example: They deliver at six in the morning.

items.meaning: a result to be handed in
items.example: The first deliverable is due in May.
Free delivery applies over ten pounds.
The delivery date was moved forward.

items.meaning: the room where babies are born
items.example: He waited outside the delivery room.
